seo.title: Notice of intention to Consider Cancellation | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: A Notice of Intention to Consider Cancellation (NOICC) is a formal notification from the Department of Home Affairs informing a visa holder that their.
seo.h1: Notice of intention to Consider Cancellation

hero.h1: Notice of intention to Consider Cancellation
intro: A Notice of Intention to Consider Cancellation (NOICC) is a formal notification from the Department of Home Affairs informing a visa holder that their visa may be cancelled. It provides the visa holder an opportunity to respond before a final cancellation decision is made.

blocks.x: What is a Notice of Intention to Consider Cancellation?

A NOICC is issued when the Department of Home Affairs is considering cancelling your visa. It outlines the reasons why cancellation is being considered and gives you a chance to provide information or reasons why your visa should not be cancelled before a final decision is made.
When is a NOICC issued?

The Department usually issues a NOICC if they believe there are grounds to cancel your visa, such as non-compliance with visa conditions, character concerns, providing false information, or other statutory reasons under the Migration Act 1958.
Your rights upon receiving a NOICC

Receiving a NOICC means you have the right to respond and present your case. You can provide evidence, explanations, or other relevant information to argue against the cancellation. This response can influence whether the Department proceeds with cancelling your visa.
How to respond to a NOICC

You should respond within the timeframe specified in the notice. Your response should address the reasons for cancellation and include any supporting documents or explanations. It is advisable to seek legal advice or assistance from a registered migration agent to prepare your response effectively.
What happens after you respond?

The Department will consider your response along with all relevant information before making a final decision. They may decide to cancel your visa or allow it to remain valid based on the merits of your case.
Consequences of visa cancellation
If your visa is cancelled, you may be required to leave Australia and could face restrictions on future visa applications. Cancellation on character grounds can lead to detention and removal.
Appeals and reviews

If your visa is cancelled, you may have the right to seek a merits review of the decision by the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), except in cases where the Minister personally made the cancellation decision. Judicial review through the courts may be available if you believe there was a legal error.
Getting help
It is strongly recommended to seek legal advice or assistance from registered migration agents or community legal services to understand your options and prepare your response to a NOICC.

sections.name: Not a decision yet
sections.h2: A NOICC is the chance to stop the cancellation

blocks.x: A notice of intention to consider cancellation means the Department is thinking about cancelling your visa. It is not the cancellation. If you do not respond, the Department can decide on the material it already has, which is the material that caused the notice.

The notice names the power, the facts they rely on, and the time you have to respond. That time is often short, sometimes a matter of days, and it is not extended because you were travelling or because you did not read the email. Answer the reasons in the notice. A long letter about your life that does not address the alleged breach is easy to put aside.

items.x: **Admit what is true.** If you did work in breach of condition 8101, or you stopped studying in breach of condition 8202, say so. A denial that the records contradict makes the rest of the letter weaker.
**Explain the circumstances.** Illness, family crisis, an employer who told you the work was allowed, or a college closure. Attach evidence, not only a statement.
**Hardship.** What happens to you, your partner and your children if the visa is cancelled, including any return to a country where you have no home.
**The future.** For a student, a current enrolment and a realistic study plan. For a sponsored worker, the employer's position and whether condition 8607 is now being met.
**Other people.** If family members hold visas that depend on yours, say what cancellation does to them.

blocks.x: Send the response by the channel the notice names, before the time stated. Keep proof it was sent. If the visa is then cancelled, the response becomes the core of any ART review. If you never responded, the Tribunal has less to work with.

sections.name: How we help
sections.h2: How we help with a NOICC

blocks.x: Call us with the notice in your hand. We would rather draft a response in two days than explain a cancellation three weeks later. We read the section number, list the documents that matter, and write a response that answers the allegations in order.

We also check whether you should keep working or studying while the notice is open. The visa is still in force until it is cancelled, but a further breach during the notice period is used against you.

faqs.a: No. A cancellation can still be recorded, and it can affect the other application. Tell us about both.

seo.title: No Further Stay Waiver | Condition 8503, 8534, 8535 | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: A No Further Stay waiver request allows visa holders in Australia to ask the Department of Home Affairs to waive the No Further Stay condition on their.

intro: A No Further Stay waiver request allows visa holders in Australia to ask the Department of Home Affairs to waive the No Further Stay condition on their visa, enabling them to apply for another visa while still in Australia under certain exceptional circumstances.

blocks.x: What is a No Further Stay condition?

A No Further Stay condition on a visa means you cannot apply for most temporary or permanent visas while you are in Australia. To apply for another visa, you usually need to leave Australia first unless you obtain a waiver of this condition.
When can you request a waiver?

You can request a waiver if there has been a major change in your situation that is beyond your control and could not have been prevented. Examples of valid reasons include medical inability to travel, death or serious illness of a close family member, natural disasters, war or civil unrest in your home country, or your school being unable to provide your approved course.

Reasons that are not valid for a waiver include marriage or starting a relationship with an Australian citizen or permanent resident, failing a course, pregnancy, or not knowing the condition was attached to your visa.
How to check if your visa has this condition
Check your visa grant letter or use the Visa Entitlement Verification Online (VEVO) service to see if your visa has a No Further Stay condition.
How to request a waiver

Submit your waiver request before your current visa expires using the No Further Stay waiver request form online. You must complete all questions and attach supporting documents such as your passport biographical page and evidence supporting your claim (e.g., medical reports). Documents not in English must be accompanied by accredited English translations.
If you cannot complete the online form, you can use Form 1447 (No Further Stay waiver request PDF).
Each visa holder must submit an individual waiver request.
After you request a waiver

Submitting a waiver request does not automatically waive the condition. The Department will assess your request and notify you of the decision. They may ask for more information, which can delay processing.
If your visa expires before a decision is made, you become unlawful and must ensure you hold a valid visa for your stay.
If the waiver is granted
You can apply for another visa while in Australia. However, there is no guarantee that the new visa application will be granted.
If the waiver is refused
You will not be able to apply for most substantive visas while in Australia. Some specified visas may still be available depending on your visa conditions.

The decision to approve or refuse a waiver is final and cannot be reviewed by the Administrative Review Tribunal. If your circumstances change significantly after refusal, you may lodge a new waiver request.

sections.name: Which condition
sections.h2: No further stay is a condition number, not a mood

blocks.x: A no-further-stay condition means you cannot apply for most other visas while you are in Australia. The common one is condition 8503, often placed on visitor visas, including sponsored family visitor visas. Student visas sometimes carry condition 8534, and student guardian visas condition 8535. The waiver rules are not identical. Read the number on your grant letter before you use a blog post written about a different condition.
Check the grant letter or VEVO. If the condition is there, lodging a partner visa, student visa or parent visa onshore will usually be invalid. The lodgement fee is not a workaround.

For condition 8503, a waiver is for a major change in your circumstances that you could not control, that happened after the visa was granted, and that is compelling and compassionate. The Department has long treated these as not enough on their own: you got married, you started a relationship, you became pregnant, you failed a course, or you did not know the condition was there.

Each person who needs the waiver lodges their own request. Use the online no-further-stay form or Form 1447 if the instructions tell you to. Lodge it while your visa is still valid. A request does not extend the visa. If the visa expires, you can be unlawful, and unlawful status creates a separate problem.
There is no ART review of a waiver refusal. If your circumstances later change in a genuine way, a new request is sometimes possible. A second request that repeats the first one is not.

items.x: We confirm the condition number and whether a waiver is even available.
We tell you if your reason is one the Department routinely rejects, before you plan a wedding around an onshore lodgement.
We prepare the request with medical or other evidence that matches the test, not with a relationship statement.
We plan the next visa only after a waiver is granted. A partner visa lodged too early is invalid.

seo.title: Applying for Work Rights | Employer sponsored visa | Work visa Australia | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: To apply for work rights in Australia, you generally need to demonstrate a compelling need, such as financial hardship, or be on an eligible.

intro: To apply for work rights in Australia, you generally need to demonstrate a compelling need, such as financial hardship, or be on an eligible employer-sponsored visa. Applications are made through the Department of Home Affairs, typically via Form 1005 or as part of your visa application process.

blocks.x: Applying for work rights on financial hardship grounds
If you need work rights due to financial hardship, you must submit Form 1005 to the Department of Home Affairs. This involves:

items.x: **Identifying the correct application:** Use the online portal or download Form 1005 from the Department’s website.

**Providing evidence of financial hardship:** Submit documents such as bank statements, bills (rent, utilities, groceries), loan or mortgage details, and if applicable, evidence of your family’s combined financial situation (e.g., if in a de facto relationship).
**Including a personal statement:** Write a detailed explanation of your circumstances and why you require work rights.
**Submitting the application:** Lodge the completed form and supporting documents online via your ImmiAccount.

blocks.x: **Important:** If you are on a student visa, applying for work rights may conflict with visa conditions requiring sufficient funds. It is advisable to consult a migration agent or lawyer before applying.
Applying for work rights on an employer-sponsored visa
If you hold an employer-sponsored visa, such as the Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482), and your sponsorship and nomination are approved, you can:

items.x: **Confirm eligibility:** Ensure your sponsorship and nomination are approved.
**Submit the application:** Apply for work rights as part of your visa application process.
**No application fee:** There is no fee for applying for work rights in this scenario.

blocks.x: Other important information

items.x: **Bridging visas:** Not all bridging visas grant work rights automatically. You may need to apply separately for permission to work.
**Protection visa holders:** If you hold a Protection visa and a Bridging visa C or E without work rights, you may be eligible to apply for a different bridging visa that includes work rights.
**Processing times:** These vary, so apply as early as possible and keep copies of all documents submitted.

sections.name: Who needs this
sections.h2: Work rights are a condition, not a favour

blocks.x: Some visas allow work. Some allow limited work. Some carry condition 8101, which means no work. You cannot assume a bridging visa copies the work rights you want. It often copies the limits of the visa you held before.

items.x: **Bridging Visa A, C or E with condition 8101.** A separate request, often on Form 1005, asks the Department to allow work because of financial hardship. You need evidence of your money, your expenses and why you cannot support yourself. A letter that says you would like to work is not hardship evidence.

**Student visa holders.** Condition 8105 already sets a work limit, currently described as 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session. Asking for unlimited work can sit badly with the requirement that you have enough money to study. Get advice before you lodge.

**Skills in Demand (482) and other sponsored visas.** You already have work rights, but condition 8607 limits you to the sponsor and the occupation. That is not changed by Form 1005. A new sponsor is a different process.
**Visitor visas and the sponsored parent visa (870).** These are no-work visas. There is no general hardship application that turns a visitor visa into a work visa.

sections.name: How we help
sections.h2: How we help you ask for work rights

blocks.x: We check whether your visa can have the condition lifted at all. If it can, we prepare Form 1005 with bank statements, bills, and a short account of who you support. If it cannot, we say so and look at whether another visa is the real answer.
Working before the condition is changed is a breach. A breach is a reason to cancel the visa and a reason to refuse the work-rights request.

faqs.a: Not if your visa has condition 8101. Wait for the grant letter that removes it.

faqs.q: Which form is it?
faqs.a: Form 1005 is the usual form for a bridging visa holder asking for work on hardship grounds. It is not the form for a new employer on a 482.

faqs.q: Will rent receipts be enough?
faqs.a: They help, but the Department looks at the whole picture: income, savings, support from family, and your expenses. One receipt does not show hardship.

seo.title: Australian Student Visa Requirements for Study Rights | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: To study in Australia, you generally need to apply for a Student visa (subclass 500), which requires acceptance into a CRICOS-registered course, obtaining.

intro: To study in Australia, you generally need to apply for a Student visa (subclass 500), which requires acceptance into a CRICOS-registered course, obtaining a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), and meeting financial and English language requirements. Applications are submitted online via ImmiAccount. For those on other visas, study rights depend on specific visa conditions.

blocks.x: Applying for study rights as a new student

items.x: **Get a Letter of Offer:** Apply to a CRICOS-registered educational institution and receive a Letter of Offer for your chosen course.
**Obtain a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE):** After accepting the offer and meeting any conditions, the institution issues a CoE, which is essential for your visa application.
**Prepare your visa application:** Gather required documents including proof of English proficiency, evidence of financial capacity to support your stay, and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC).
**Create an ImmiAccount:** Set up an account on the Department of Home Affairs website to submit and manage your visa application.
**Submit your Student visa (subclass 500) application:** Lodge the application online through your ImmiAccount.
**Monitor your application:** Regularly check your ImmiAccount for updates or requests for additional information.

blocks.x: For students holding other visas

items.x: **Bridging Visa E holders:** Check your visa conditions carefully, as this visa may restrict your ability to study. You often need permission from the Department of Home Affairs before enrolling in courses.

**Other visa holders:** Study rights vary depending on your visa type. Always review your visa conditions and seek advice from the Department or a migration lawyer if unsure about your eligibility to study.

blocks.x: Important considerations

items.x: Ensure your course is CRICOS-registered to be eligible for a Student visa.
Maintain compliance with visa conditions to avoid cancellation or refusal.
Seek professional advice if you have complex visa circumstances or need to extend study rights.

blocks.x: Study rights are written on the visa as conditions. They are not added by enrolling at a college.

items.x: **Visitor visas.** Condition 8201 usually limits study or training to three months. A longer course needs a student visa, not a quiet enrolment.
**Bridging visas.** Some allow study and some do not. The bridging visa grant letter controls it. A Bridging Visa A that came from a visitor visa may keep the three-month limit.

**Student visas.** You may study, but condition 8202 requires you to remain enrolled and meet course progress and attendance. Changing course has its own rules. See [course change](/study-australia/course-change-in-australia) and the [student visa](/study-australia/student-visa-subclass-500).

**Sponsored workers.** Condition 8607 limits your work. Study on the side is possible only if it does not break your work condition or a condition such as 8101. A Skills in Demand visa is not a student visa.

intro: A bridging visa lets you stay in Australia lawfully while the Department of Home Affairs decides another application. faqs.q: What is a bridging visa?
faqs.a: A bridging visa is a temporary visa that lets you stay in Australia lawfully while the Department decides another visa application or while a review is in progress. It is not a visa you apply to stay on forever.

faqs.q: Do I need to apply for a Bridging Visa A?
faqs.a: Usually not. In most cases it is granted automatically when you lodge a valid substantive visa application in Australia while holding a substantive visa. Read the [Bridging Visa A page](/bridging-return-visas/bridging-visa-a-010) for the details.

faqs.q: Can I travel overseas on a bridging visa?
faqs.a: Not on a Bridging Visa A, B or C unless you hold a Bridging Visa B or a travel facility. Leaving Australia without the right visa can end your bridging visa and your right to return. Get advice before you book a flight.

faqs.q: Can I work on a bridging visa?
faqs.a: It depends on the visa and its conditions. Bridging Visa A usually carries the same work and study conditions as your previous visa. Bridging Visa C and E often limit work. Check your visa grant notice.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Bridging Visa A and Bridging Visa C?
faqs.a: You get a Bridging Visa A when you apply while your last visa is still valid. You get a Bridging Visa C when you apply after it has ended. The work, study and travel consequences are different.

faqs.q: What is a Resident Return visa?
faqs.a: It is a visa for permanent residents who want to return to Australia after the travel facility on their permanent visa has ended. See the [Resident Return page](/bridging-return-visas/resident-return-visa-155-157).

faqs.q: My visa was cancelled. What can I do?
faqs.a: You may have review rights with strict deadlines. Contact us straight away. See [Visa Cancellation](/appeals/visa-cancellation).

faqs.q: Do you guarantee a bridging visa?
faqs.a: No. Only the Department of Home Affairs decides. We tell you honestly what is realistic before you spend money.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a Maritime Crew visa and a Crew Travel Authority?
faqs.a: A Maritime Crew visa (988) is for crew arriving by sea on eligible ships. A Crew Travel Authority (942) is for airline crew and aircraft safety inspectors arriving by air. They are separate documents for separate kinds of travel.

faqs.q: Does crew need a visa to enter Australia?

blocks.x: Study can be part of a pathway to permanent residence, but it is never automatic.

items.x: **Choose a course.** Pick a CRICOS-registered course that fits your past study, work and future plans. See [Admission in Australia](/study-australia/admission-in-australia).
**Get your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).** Your provider issues it after you accept your offer. See [New CoE](/study-australia/new-coe).

sections.name: Reality checks
sections.h2: What to know before you commit

items.x: **No automatic PR.** Graduating does not guarantee permanent residency. Skilled visas depend on your occupation, skills assessment, points and invitation or nomination.
**Genuine Student scrutiny.** The Department looks at whether your course is a logical step from your past study and work, and whether you intend to study.
**Costs are real.** Tuition, living costs, health cover and the visa charge must be planned. Work income should help with living costs, not be your plan for paying tuition.
**Changing provider early.** In the first six months of your main course you may need a release letter from your provider.
**Rules change.** Student visa settings have changed often in recent years, including fees, funds and who can apply from inside Australia.

sections.name: The Genuine Student requirement and funds
sections.h2: The two things that decide most student visa applications

blocks.x: **Genuine Student (GS) requirement.** You answer written questions about your circumstances, why you chose this course and provider, what you will gain in your career, and your immigration history. Clear, honest, personal answers that match your documents work best. Copied or generic answers cause problems.

**Funds.** You show you can pay for tuition, living costs and travel for yourself and any family members. The required amount has risen in recent years. We do not quote a figure here because it changes. Use our [Student Visa Financial Calculator](/study-australia/student-visa-financial-calculator) for an estimate.
**English.** Many courses ask for IELTS, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT or similar.
Estimate the funds you may need to show for a Subclass 500 visa. The result is an estimate only.

items.x: **Talk.** Tell us your background, budget and goals.
**Plan.** We explain your course options and what the visa will ask of you.
**Apply.** We help with admission documents and your visa application, as set out in your written service agreement.
**Follow up.** We help you meet your conditions, respond to Department requests and plan the next visa.

blocks.x: Visa advice is given by registered migration agents. You can check each agent on the OMARA register. See [our registrations](/study-australia/our-affiliations). [Book a study consultation](/book-an-appointment).

faqs.q: What is the Subclass 500 student visa?
faqs.a: It lets you stay in Australia to study a full-time CRICOS-registered course. You need a Confirmation of Enrolment, health cover, English, funds and to meet the Genuine Student requirement.

faqs.q: Can I work on a student visa?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. During your course you can work up to a set number of hours each fortnight, and more in official course breaks. Work is meant to support living costs.

faqs.q: Will studying in Australia get me PR?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Some graduates may become eligible for a graduate visa or a skilled visa. This depends on your occupation, skills assessment, points and current rules. A registered agent can check your case.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to show?
faqs.a: You need to show funds for tuition, living costs and travel. The living-cost figure changes. Try our financial calculator for an estimate.

faqs.q: Can I change my course after I arrive?
faqs.a: Often yes, but the rules depend on the level of the new course and how long you have studied. Read our [course change page](/study-australia/course-change-in-australia) first.

faqs.q: Can my family come with me?
faqs.a: Only if an exemption applies, and only in the same application. You cannot add them after the student visa is granted. A parent of a student under 18 may still qualify for a guardian visa. See [family on a student visa](/study-australia/student-dependent-visa-500) and the [guardian visa](/study-australia/student-guardian-visa-590).

faqs.q: Do you guarantee a student visa?
faqs.a: No. Only the Department of Home Affairs decides. We tell you honestly how strong your plan looks.

seo.description: Dreaming of studying in Australia? This streamlined guide helps you choose the right course, meet academic and English requirements, secure your.

intro: Dreaming of studying in Australia? This streamlined guide helps you choose the right course, meet academic and English requirements, secure your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), and apply for the Student Visa (subclass 500).

blocks.x: **Introduction**

Planning to study in Australia starts with a clear path: pick a course that fits your goals, meet the entry and English requirements, and complete a strong Student Visa (subclass 500) application. With the right preparation, you can turn your study plans into reality.
**Choose Your Course and Meet Entry Requirements**

Start by exploring programs, locations, providers, and fees using the official Study Australia course search. Review each course’s prerequisites and prepare certified academic transcripts and proof of grades or GPA. If you’re applying from high school, your ATAR may be considered for undergraduate entry. You’ll also need to demonstrate English proficiency with an accepted test such as IELTS, PTE Academic, or TOEFL iBT. Many programs look for an overall IELTS score of 6.5 with no band below 6.0, though competitive fields like nursing, education, or law may require higher scores.
**Secure Your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)**

After you receive and accept your offer, your education provider will issue a CoE—this is the cornerstone document for your Student Visa (subclass 500). Ensure you’ve met all conditions and paid required deposits so your CoE can be generated without delays.
**Prepare for Visa Requirements**

To apply for the Student Visa (subclass 500), show that you’re a genuine student with a clear study plan aligned to your background and goals. Demonstrate financial capacity to cover tuition, living expenses, and travel, and arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for your entire stay. Have the essentials ready: a valid passport, certified transcripts, English test results, CoE, OSHC policy details, and any additional documents requested for your situation.
**Submit Your Visa Application**

When you’re ready, prepare clean, legible copies of your documents in English (include certified translations if needed) and keep both originals and translations. Lodge your Student Visa (subclass 500) online via the Australian Department of Home Affairs, pay the required fees, submit your application, and monitor your email for any requests for additional information.
**Tips for a Smooth Process**

Start early to allow time for testing, document certification, and processing. Schedule your English test ahead of deadlines, and ensure your personal details and study story are consistent across your CoE, Statement of Purpose, and financial documents. Keep OSHC active from your arrival through to your visa end date. With careful planning, you’ll be ready to begin your Australian study adventure with confidence.

seo.description: Need a new Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) in Australia? Here’s a clear, student-friendly guide on when you need a new CoE, how to apply through your.

intro: Need a new Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) in Australia? Here’s a clear, student-friendly guide on when you need a new CoE, how to apply through your institution’s portal, what documents to prepare, why you must align your OSHC, and how to use the new CoE to extend your Student Visa (subclass 500) on time.

blocks.x: **What Is a “New CoE” and Why It Matters**

A new Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) is an official document issued by your education provider that confirms your continued enrolment. International students need a valid CoE to apply for or renew a Student Visa (subclass 500). If your study plan changes or your current CoE is expiring before you finish, you must get a new CoE to stay compliant and avoid visa issues.
**When You Need a New CoE**
**You should apply for a new CoE if:**

items.x: You need to extend your student visa because your course end date has moved.
You change your program of study, especially if you move to a lower AQF qualification level.
Your current CoE or visa will expire before you complete your course requirements.

blocks.x: Apply at least 10 working days before you need it to ensure it’s issued in time.
**How to Apply for a New CoE**

items.x: Apply via your institution’s portal: Log in to your university or college online portal and submit the CoE application as instructed. Follow any faculty or international office guidelines carefully.
Extend your OSHC: If you’re extending your visa, update your Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) so it covers your new study period. Your Coe dates and OSHC should align.
Submit only once: Avoid multiple submissions as they can slow down processing or create duplicates.
Provide supporting documents: Upload any required evidence, such as updated course plans or documents for compassionate/compelling circumstances (e.g., medical certificates, academic advice).
Allow processing time: Processing can take up to 10 working days. Apply early to avoid gaps in your visa status.

blocks.x: **After You Receive Your New Coe**

items.x: Check your email: Your provider will send the new Coe to your registered email. Verify the details (course, start/end dates, CRICOS provider).
Apply for your visa extension: Use the new Coe to lodge a Student Visa (subclass 500) extension via the Department of Home Affairs online system.
Mind the start date: You must submit your visa application before the course start date listed on the new Coe.

blocks.x: **Pro Tips**

items.x: Keep consistency: Ensure your new Coe dates, OSHC policy dates, and visa application details match.
Start early: Build in buffer time for any back-and-forth with your institution or insurer.
Save everything: Keep copies of your CoE, OSHC receipt, and supporting documents for your visa application and future reference.

blocks.x: **Note:** Requirements can vary by provider. Always follow your institution’s specific instructions and refer to the Australian Department of Home Affairs for current visa guidance.

intro: Thinking of changing your course in Australia? Here’s a clear guide on switching within the same provider or moving to a new one, when you’ll need a new CoE or a new student visa, and the key rules to stay compliant especially around AQF levels, the first six months restriction, and CRICOS registration.

blocks.x: **Changing Courses in Australia: What to Know**

If you want to change courses, start by speaking with your current education provider. The steps you’ll follow depend on whether your new course is at the same/higher AQF level, a lower level, and whether you’re staying with the same provider or transferring to a new one. In all cases, you’ll need a new Confirmation of Enrolment (Coe) for the new course and must ensure your visa remains valid.
**If You Stay with Your Current Provider**

If you plan to remain at the same institution, book time with a student advisor or course coordinator to understand internal processes, any fees, and how your study plan will be updated. You’ll receive a new CoE for the new course:

items.x: New course at the same or higher level: You can usually switch without applying for a new visa. Your provider will issue a new CoE and update Home Affairs.
New course at a lower level: You’ll need to apply for a new Student Visa (subclass 500). Changing to a lower AQF level without a new visa may breach visa conditions.

blocks.x: **If You Change Providers**
If you’re moving to a different institution, timing matters:

items.x: Less than six months into your main course: You typically must obtain a release letter from your current provider and provide compelling reasons for the transfer. Check your provider’s release policy and documentation requirements.

More than six months of study: You can generally transfer without needing approval from your current institution. However, if your new course is at a lower AQF level, you’ll likely need to apply for a new student visa.

blocks.x: **General Requirements and Compliance**

items.x: CRICOS registration: Your new course must be CRICOS-registered.
New CoE required: Secure a valid CoE for the new course before you change.
Avoid study gaps: Ensure there’s no gap between your old and new courses that could affect your visa status.
Visa alignment: If extending study time, align your OSHC coverage with your new course/visa dates.
Check official guidance: Requirements can vary by visa subclass and personal circumstances. Always verify details on the Department of Home Affairs website and follow your provider’s policies.

seo.h1: What is Recognized Prior Learning (RPL), Australia?

hero.h1: What is Recognized Prior Learning (RPL), Australia?
intro: Recognized Prior Learning (RPL) lets you turn your real-world experience into nationally recognized qualifications in Australia. By matching your existing skills and knowledge to the competency standards of a qualification, you can earn credit, finish faster, and pay less without re-learning what you already know.

blocks.x: **What Is RPL?**

Recognized Prior Learning (RPL) is an assessment pathway that evaluates the skills, knowledge, and experience you’ve gained through work, volunteering, training, or life experience against the requirements of a formal qualification. If you already meet the competencies for certain units, you can receive credit toward a nationally recognized qualification.
**How RPL Works**

items.x: Assessment: A qualified assessor maps your existing skills and knowledge to the units of competency in your chosen qualification.
Evidence: You provide proof of competency such as work samples, portfolios, position descriptions, references, performance reviews, training certificates, and testimonials.
Validation: Assessors check that your evidence is authentic, valid, current, reliable, and sufficient to meet each unit’s requirements.
Outcome: You may be granted credit for some or all units. If gaps are found, your assessor will outline what is still required (e.g., targeted training or additional evidence).

blocks.x: **Benefits of RPL**

items.x: Save time and money: Reduce study duration and tuition by receiving credit for what you already know and can do.
Career advancement: Gain a credential that supports promotions, career changes, or entry into higher-level study.
Formal recognition: Convert informal and on-the-job learning into a nationally recognized qualification.
Job security and mobility: A formal qualification can strengthen your employability and broaden opportunities across industries.

blocks.x: **Who Is Eligible?**

Anyone with relevant skills and knowledge from work, previous study (formal or informal), volunteering, or life experience can be considered. Eligibility depends on the industry, the specific qualification, and how well your experience aligns with the required competencies.
**Getting Started**

items.x: Choose a qualification: Ensure its nationally recognized and delivered by an RTO (Registered Training Organisation).
Speak with the provider: Request an RPL information pack and a pre-assessment to understand evidence requirements.
Gather evidence: Compile documents and examples that best demonstrate your experience and outcomes.
Submit and assess: Lodge your RPL application; respond quickly to any requests for additional information.
Fill any gaps: Complete targeted training or workplace tasks if partial RPL is recommended.

blocks.x: **Tip:** To speed up your RPL, organise your evidence by unit and clearly label documents to show how each piece maps to the competency requirements.

seo.description: A Professional Year Program (PYP) is a 44–52 week job-readiness pathway for international graduates in Australia, blending classroom learning with a.

intro: A Professional Year Program (PYP) is a 44–52 week job-readiness pathway for international graduates in Australia, blending classroom learning with a 12-week internship. It builds industry skills, Australian workplace readiness, and can add five points towards permanent residency, especially valuable in accounting, IT, and engineering.

blocks.x: **What Is a Professional Year Program?**

A Professional Year Program is a structured, post-study pathway designed to help international graduates transition from university to the Australian workforce. Over approximately 44 to 52 weeks, you’ll complete targeted professional training plus a supervised 12-week internship that delivers real workplace experience in your field. PYPs are commonly available for accounting, information technology, and engineering graduates of Australian universities.
**Key Components**

items.x: Formal learning: Classroom-based modules covering industry tools, professional standards and ethics, communication, job search strategies, and interview skills.
Workplace experience: A 12-week internship in an Australian company to apply your skills, build confidence, and understand day-to-day operations and expectations.
Cultural capability: Practical training to navigate Australian workplace culture collaboration, feedback, communication styles, and professional etiquette.

blocks.x: **Benefits**

items.x: Job-ready skills: Develop targeted, industry-specific competencies and soft skills valued by Australian employers.
Local experience: Gain hands-on experience and references that strengthen your resume and LinkedIn profile.
Career momentum: Improve employability, expand your professional network, and access potential job offers from your host company or industry contacts.
Migration advantage: Successful completion can provide five points toward Australia’s permanent residency (subject to current migration rules).

seo.description: Requesting a study deferral is usually done through your university’s online portal using a Deferral Request Form. Policies vary by institution and.

intro: Requesting a study deferral is usually done through your university’s online portal using a Deferral Request Form. Policies vary by institution and course, so always follow the instructions in your offer letter and admissions page. After you submit, you’ll receive an outcome by email, and your CoE may be updated if approved.

blocks.x: **What Is a Study Deferral?**

A study deferral allows you to postpone your course start date to a later intake. The availability, duration, and conditions of deferral differ by university and program, so it’s essential to check your offer letter and the university’s admissions website for exact rules and deadlines.
**Steps to Request a Deferral**

items.x: **Locate the correct form:** Log in to your university’s applicant or student portal and find the Deferral Request Form. Access often becomes available after receiving your offer.
**Complete the form:** Enter your personal details, application or student ID, and nominate your preferred new start date or intake.
**Submit the form:** Lodge the request through the portal. Some universities require you to accept your offer first; others let you request a deferral as part of responding to the offer.
**Receive confirmation:** Watch your email for the decision and any next steps.
**Check for updates:**If approved, your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) may be updated, and you’ll receive enrolment instructions closer to your new start date.

blocks.x: **Important Considerations**

items.x: **Deferral limits:** Maximum periods vary. Many undergraduate programs allow up to two years; some postgraduate or online programs cap deferral at one year.

**Course restrictions:** Deferral may not be available for all programs particularly limited/quota courses, some honours years, or regulated professional programs (e.g., Medicine, Psychology), as noted by universities like Deakin and UNE.
**Policy changes:** You’ll study under the rules in effect in the year you commence after deferral, which may differ from those when you first received your offer.
**Visa and CoE alignment:** International students should ensure their CoE and visa timelines align with the new start date; update OSHC if needed.
**Contact the university:** If anything is unclear, reach out to admissions or the future students team for guidance and deadlines.

blocks.x: Tip: Submit your deferral request as early as possible places in future intakes can fill quickly, and processing times vary by institution and time of year.

Work and study rights are generally not granted (limited study may be possible; no work unless exceptional circumstances).

seo.title: Student Visa Subclass 500 | Requirements and How to Apply | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: Student visa (subclass 500): Confirmation of Enrolment, Genuine Student requirement, funds, English, OSHC, the visa charge and what to do after you are granted.

intro: The Student visa (subclass 500) lets you study full-time in Australia on a CRICOS-registered course. You need a Confirmation of Enrolment, Overseas Student Health Cover, and evidence of English, funds, health and character. You must also meet the Genuine Student requirement. This page covers who can apply, what to prepare, how to lodge, and what happens after the visa is granted.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Full-time CRICOS course, with a Confirmation of Enrolment
Required for applications lodged on or after 23 March 2024
AUD 2,500 for most students. Some sectors and passports pay less
Usually limited while your course is in session. Check the grant letter
A Temporary Graduate visa (485) may be available if you qualify

sections.name: Requirements
sections.h2: What you need before you apply

blocks.x: Start with the course, then the visa. The Department of Home Affairs decides the visa. Your education provider decides the offer.

items.x: **Choose a CRICOS course and accept the offer.** Pay any deposit the provider asks for. The provider then issues a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).
**Arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)** for the whole stay, for you and any family members on the application.
**Show English.** The level depends on the course. Common tests include IELTS, PTE and TOEFL. Some applicants are exempt. Your provider and Home Affairs can require different levels.

**Show you can pay for the course, living costs and travel.** Use the [Student Visa Financial Calculator](/study-australia/student-visa-financial-calculator) for an estimate. The living-cost figure changes, so check it before you lodge.
**Meet health and character requirements.** Home Affairs may ask for a medical examination and police certificates.
**Write a Genuine Student statement.** Explain why you chose this course in Australia, how it follows your past study or work, and what you plan to do with the qualification.

blocks.x: Applications lodged on or after 23 March 2024 are assessed under the Genuine Student requirement, not the old Genuine Temporary Entrant test. You must be a genuine applicant for entry and stay as a student, and studying in Australia must be your primary reason for the visa. A later plan to apply for another visa, including permanent residence, does not by itself count against you. Home Affairs looks at your circumstances, your immigration history, and, if you are under 18, the intentions of a parent or guardian. The Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) is different: the guardian is still assessed as a genuine temporary entrant.

items.x: **Get the CoE and collect the evidence.** Passport, CoE, English results, financial evidence, OSHC and the Genuine Student statement.
**Lodge in ImmiAccount.** Complete the subclass 500 application, upload the documents and pay the visa application charge.
**Respond if Home Affairs asks for more.** That can include biometrics, a health examination or police certificates. Answer before the date in the request.
**Check the grant.** Use VEVO for the conditions and the expiry date. Keep your provider and Home Affairs updated if your details change.

blocks.x: From 2 October 2026 there are extra limits on who can apply for a Student visa while in Australia, and on including family members. Read the current [Home Affairs student visa page](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500) before you lodge.

items.x: Stay enrolled and meet course progress and attendance.
Keep OSHC current for everyone on the visa.

Follow the work condition on your grant. For many students that is up to 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session, with more hours in official breaks. A masters by research or a doctoral degree can be different.

Tell your provider before you defer, change course or take a break. See [course change](/study-australia/course-change-in-australia) and [deferring your studies](/study-australia/request-to-defer-your-studies).
If you need to keep studying after this visa ends, you lodge a new Student visa. See [student visa extension](/study-australia/student-visa-extension).

Family members are not automatic. See [family on a student visa](/study-australia/student-dependent-visa-500). A parent caring for a student under 18 may need a [Student Guardian visa (590)](/study-australia/student-guardian-visa-590).
Near the end of the course, check whether a [Temporary Graduate visa (485)](/migrate-to-australia/temporary-graduate-visa-subclass-485) is open to you. It is a separate application.

What it covers
rows: Schools, vocational education, higher education and postgraduate research
On a schools, vocational or higher education application
Base charge. Additional applicant 18 or over is AUD 1,255. Under 18 is AUD 410.
Foreign Affairs, Defence, or secondary exchange
No base charge for these sectors

blocks.x: These amounts are from the Department of Home Affairs [current visa pricing table](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing), checked November 2026. Some passport holders pay a lower charge. Tuition, OSHC and living costs are separate. Include family members in the first application if they need a visa.

There is no set processing time. Use the Department of Home Affairs [visa processing time guide](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-processing-times/global-visa-processing-times). It shows how long recent applications took. It is a guide only, not a promise for your application.

sections.name: Common refusal reasons
sections.h2: Common reasons these applications are refused

blocks.x: Student visa refusals are usually about the Genuine Student test, money, or English.

items.x: **The course does not fit** your background, or the statement reads as a copy.
**Funds** are borrowed at the last minute or are not really available.
**English** is below the requirement.
**A previous student visa** was cancelled, or a gap in study is not explained.
**The provider or the course** is not CRICOS.

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record. If you already have a refusal letter, read [visa refusal](/appeals/visa-refusal) and check the deadline before you reapply.
Condition 8202 and condition 8105 are the two conditions that lead to student cancellations.

items.x: **8202.** Stay enrolled, meet course progress and meet attendance.

**8105.** The work limit is set on the grant letter. It has been 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session. The number can change. Work is not limited in the same way during scheduled breaks.
**8501.** Keep Overseas Student Health Cover.
**8516.** You must continue to be eligible for the visa.
**8534** on some grants stops you applying for most other visas in Australia, other than another student visa.
**8532** applies to many students under 18: welfare and accommodation arrangements.

blocks.x: The numbers on your grant letter control what you can do. If a condition is breached, the visa can be cancelled. See [visa cancellation](/appeals/visa-cancellation) and, if you have a notice, [notice of intention to consider cancellation](/appeals/notice-of-intention-to-consider-cancellation).

faqs.q: What replaced the Genuine Temporary Entrant test?
faqs.a: For a Student visa lodged on or after 23 March 2024, the Genuine Student requirement replaced the Genuine Temporary Entrant test. A Student Guardian visa (subclass 590) is still assessed as a genuine temporary entrant.

faqs.q: Can I work on a student visa?
faqs.a: Usually yes, with a limit while your course is in session. Many grants allow 48 hours a fortnight in session and unlimited hours in official breaks. Read the conditions on your grant letter.

faqs.q: Does a student visa lead to permanent residence?

blocks.x: **Pre‑Application Steps**

Begin by applying to your chosen education provider and, once accepted, review and accept your Letter of Offer. After meeting any conditions and paying required deposits, your institution will issue a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE). Next, gather all supporting documents: proof of English proficiency (e.g., IELTS/PTE/TOEFL), financial capacity to cover tuition, living and travel, a valid passport, and any required health and character checks. Prepare a strong Genuine Student (GS) statement that clearly explains your study intent, course relevance, and future plans.
**Visa Application and Processing**

Create or log in to ImmiAccount and complete the online Student visa (Subclass 500) application. Upload your CoE, English results, financial evidence, OSHC policy, ID, and any other requested documents, then pay the application fee. You may be asked to undertake a medical examination, provide biometrics, and supply police certificates. Processing times vary; some applications are decided in several weeks, while others can take a few months depending on case complexity and completeness. Monitor your account and respond quickly to any requests for further information.
**Post‑Visa Approval and Next Steps**

Once granted, comply with all visa conditions, including maintaining enrolment, achieving satisfactory course progress and attendance, holding valid OSHC, and adhering to work limits while your course is in session. Keep your details current with your provider and Home Affairs. As you near course completion, consider future options such as the Temporary Graduate visa (Subclass 485) to gain post‑study work experience, or explore skilled, employer‑sponsored, or further study pathways depending on your goals and eligibility.

hero.badge: Registered migration agents, Melbourne and Adelaide
intro: A skills assessment is the check by an Australian assessing authority that your qualification and work match an occupation on the relevant list. Most skilled visas, including 189, 190, 491 and many employer visas, need a positive assessment before you can be invited or nominated.

blocks.x: Your Complete Skills Assessment Guide

A skills assessment is a critical step in your Australian immigration journey. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know about skills assessments, from understanding what they are to successfully completing your application.
Understanding Skills Assessments

A skills assessment is an official evaluation by a designated Australian assessing authority that verifies your qualifications and work experience are suitable for your nominated occupation. This assessment is mandatory for most skilled migration visa pathways, including:

items.x: **Skilled Independent Visa (189):** Points-tested permanent residence
**Skilled Nominated Visa (190):** State-nominated permanent residence
**Skilled Work Regional Visa (491):** Regional provisional visa
**Temporary Graduate Visa (485):** Post-study work rights
**Skills in Demand visa (482):** Employer-sponsored work visa
**Employer Nomination Scheme (186):** Permanent employer sponsorship

blocks.x: Major Assessing Authorities in Australia
**For:** ICT and technology professionals
Assesses qualifications and experience for software engineers, developers, IT managers, business analysts, and other ICT occupations.
**For:** Engineering professionals
Assesses all engineering disciplines including civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, and software engineering.
**For:** General professional occupations
Covers over 350 professional occupations including managers, marketing professionals, HR specialists, and more.
**For:** Trade occupations
Assesses trade qualifications for electricians, plumbers, carpenters, chefs, hairdressers, and other skilled trades.
**For:** Nursing and midwifery professionals
Assesses nursing qualifications and provides pathway to AHPRA registration for nurses and midwives.
**For:** Accounting professionals
Assesses accountants, auditors, and finance professionals for migration purposes.
Document Requirements - What You'll Need
Most assessing authorities require certified copies of documents, not originals. Documents can be certified by a Justice of Peace, notary public, or other authorized certifiers.

items.x: Degree/diploma certificates (all tertiary qualifications)
Complete academic transcripts showing all subjects and grades
Course curriculum or syllabus (if required by authority)
Trade certificates and apprenticeship documents (for trades)
Detailed employment references on company letterhead
Job descriptions and responsibilities
Payslips (usually 2-3 per year of employment)
Tax returns or group certificates
Employment contracts
Organizational charts (if available)
Current passport (bio-data page)
English language test results (IELTS/PTE/TOEFL)
Professional registration certificates (if applicable)
CPD/continuing education records
Published papers or portfolio (for some professions)

blocks.x: Common Mistakes to Avoid
Employment references must include specific details: job title, employment dates, duties performed, hours worked, and supervisor contact details. Generic references often lead to delays or refusals.
Ensure all documents are clear, legible, and properly certified. Poor quality scans or uncertified documents will be rejected.
Each occupation has a specific assessing authority. Applying to the wrong one wastes time and money. Always check the official skilled occupation list first.
Most authorities require a minimum period of skilled work experience in your nominated occupation. Ensure you meet the requirements before applying.
Tips for a Successful Application
Begin gathering documents months before you plan to apply. Some employers may take time to provide references, and overseas documents may need translation.
Employment references are the most scrutinized documents. Ensure they are detailed, on letterhead, signed by a manager, and include all required information.
Each authority has unique requirements. Read the guidelines carefully and ensure you meet all criteria before submitting your application.
A registered migration agent can review your documents, ensure completeness, and maximize your chances of a positive outcome on the first attempt.
After Your Assessment
Once you receive a positive skills assessment, you can proceed with your visa application. Your assessment is typically valid for 3 years, during which you can:

items.x: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for points-tested visas
Apply for state nomination (subclass 190/491)
Use it for employer-sponsored visa applications
Apply for multiple visa applications using the same assessment

blocks.x: Assessment Pathways

hero.badge: Registered migration agents, Melbourne and Adelaide
intro: VETASSESS provides skills assessment services for migration to Australia, evaluating the qualifications, skills, and experience of professionals and tradespeople across a wide range of occupations. This assessment is a key requirement for skilled migration applications.

blocks.x: Skills Assessment for Migration

Getting your skills assessed by VETASSESS is essential if you plan to migrate to Australia under skilled migration programs. VETASSESS assesses both professional and trade occupations to verify that your skills and qualifications meet Australian standards.
Occupation categories

items.x: **For Professionals:** VETASSESS assesses over 340 professional occupations across various industries, including marketing professionals, management consultants, cafe or restaurant managers, and internal auditors.
**For Trades:** VETASSESS assesses 27 trade occupations such as cooks, chefs, electricians, motor mechanics, and welders.

**Match:** Ensure your skills and experience align with the chosen occupation.

For employers and businesses, VETASSESS offers services to address skills shortages, upskill employees, and assess workforce capabilities.

sections.name: What VETASSESS does
sections.h2: Professional occupations, and a smaller trade list

blocks.x: VETASSESS is the assessing authority for a large group of general professional occupations that do not have their own authority. Marketing specialists, management consultants, graphic designers, hotel managers and many other codes sit here. It also assesses a smaller list of trade occupations. If your occupation is ICT, engineering, accounting, nursing, teaching or medicine, you are usually with a different authority. Start with the [skills assessment hub](/skill-assessment) if you are not sure.

A VETASSESS full skills assessment looks at your qualification and at whether your employment is at the right skill level and closely related to the occupation. A points-test advice outcome, where VETASSESS offers it, is a different product. It can help you understand the years of employment you might claim in SkillSelect. It is not always a substitute for the full assessment your visa needs. Read the current VETASSESS instructions for your occupation before you choose a product.

Employment is usually counted only when it was paid, at least 20 hours a week, and closely related. Work you did before you finished the qualification is often not counted, or is counted at a reduced rate. Casual work, unpaid family work and duties that do not match the ANZSCO description are the usual reasons a year of experience disappears.

items.x: Passport and the qualification documents: parchment and full academic transcript, translated by NAATI if required.
Employer statements that list duties, dates, hours and whether the work was paid. The duties should be specific enough to match the occupation, not a one-line job title.
Evidence the work was paid: tax, payslips, superannuation or the equivalent from that country.
A résumé that uses the same dates. Do not round employment up to the nearest year.
Any licence or registration the occupation requires in Australia or in the country where you worked.

blocks.x: VETASSESS publishes its own fees and processing times and changes them. We do not treat a figure on a third-party page as current. Check VETASSESS before you pay, and see our [timeline](/skill-assessment/timeline) only as a companion.

sections.name: Common refusal reasons
sections.h2: Common reasons these applications are refused

blocks.x: A negative VETASSESS result is about the criteria for that occupation. It is not a Department visa refusal, but it will block a skilled visa that needs a positive assessment.

items.x: **The qualification is not comparable** to the Australian level the occupation needs, or it is in an unrelated field.
**The duties match a different occupation,** so the years you hoped to claim are assessed as not closely related.
**The work was part time, unpaid, or before the qualification,** and the authority's rules exclude it.
**The employment dates are not proved.** A reference without payment evidence is often given little weight.
**The wrong VETASSESS product was lodged,** and the outcome cannot be used for the visa you want.

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record. If you already have a refusal letter, read [visa refusal](/appeals/visa-refusal) and check the deadline before you reapply.

A positive full assessment is an input to an expression of interest for a [189](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189), [190](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190) or [491](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491), or to some employer visas. It has an expiry. Do not let it lapse while you wait for an invitation and assume it can be extended for free.

If the result is negative, look at the review option VETASSESS offered in the letter and the date. A new application with the same documents and a different story is a poor plan. If the occupation itself was wrong, a new application with a different authority may be the honest path.

faqs.a: No. ICT occupations are assessed by ACS. Lodging an IT occupation with VETASSESS is the wrong authority.

faqs.q: Is a full assessment the same as points test advice?
faqs.a: No. Points test advice, where it is offered, comments on employment for the points test. Your visa may still need a full skills assessment. Check the current VETASSESS product list for your occupation.

faqs.q: How many hours a week count?
faqs.a: VETASSESS generally looks for paid work of at least 20 hours a week in a closely related role. Shorter hours are a common reason a period is not counted.

faqs.q: Can I claim work from before I graduated?
faqs.a: Often that work is not counted, or it is counted in a limited way. It depends on the occupation and the current VETASSESS rules.

faqs.q: What if my result is negative?
faqs.a: Read the reasons and the review deadline in the letter. Sending the same file again rarely changes the outcome.

intro: Engineers Australia conducts migration skills assessments for engineers who wish to migrate to Australia. As the government‑authorised assessing authority, Engineers Australia evaluates qualifications, skills and professional experience and issues a skills assessment outcome letter required for visa applications.

blocks.x: If you want to migrate to Australia as an engineer, you must obtain a migration skills assessment from Engineers Australia. This assessment confirms whether your tertiary qualifications and professional experience meet Australian standards for your nominated engineering occupation and provides the outcome letter you will include with your Department of Home Affairs visa application.
Recent change for advanced diplomas and associate degrees

Effective 1 September 2024, Engineers Australia updated its approach to assessing advanced diploma and associate degree qualifications from Registered Training Organisations (RTOs). Applicants with these qualifications should check the revised requirements before applying, as assessment pathways or evidence requirements may differ from those for bachelor’s and higher degrees.
Six‑step assessment process
Applying for a skills assessment is structured into six steps:

items.x: Check your qualification — verify that your qualification is recognised and matches an engineering occupation the organisation assesses.

Understand the four engineering occupational categories — determine which occupational category (e.g., Professional Engineer, Engineering Technologist, Engineering Associate, or Engineering Manager) best fits your qualifications and experience.
Choose an assessment pathway — select the appropriate pathway (e.g., accredited qualification, competence demonstration, or recognition of prior learning) based on your education and work history.
Prepare your application — gather required documents (academic transcripts, certified qualifications, employment references, CV, and any additional evidence relevant to your chosen pathway).
Submit your application — lodge your application and pay the applicable fees through Engineers Australia’s online portal.
Receive the outcome — Engineers Australia will assess your submission and issue an outcome letter. If successful, this letter is used for migration visa applications.

blocks.x: Preparing your application and documentation

Thorough preparation improves the likelihood of a smooth assessment. Provide clear, certified copies of academic records, detailed employment references that specify duties and dates, and any evidence of continuing professional development. If your documents are not in English, include accredited translations.
Occupational categories and choosing the right one

Engineers Australia assesses applicants against four broad occupational categories; selecting the correct category is essential because it determines the competencies and evidence required. Use Engineers Australia guidance and the online quiz/tool to help match your qualifications and role to the appropriate occupation.
Assessment pathways and eligibility

Different pathways exist depending on whether your qualification is accredited in Australia (or recognised under international accords), obtained overseas, or if you are relying on substantial work experience in lieu of formal qualifications. Read the pathway criteria carefully to ensure you submit the correct evidence and choose the correct application type.
Outcome reviews and appeals

If you disagree with an assessment decision, Engineers Australia provides information on outcome review and appeal processes. Timeframes and grounds for review vary — check the published policy and submit any requests within the specified deadlines.
Processing times, fees and support

Processing times and fees vary by pathway and application complexity. Applicants can view current processing times on the Engineers Australia website. For help, contact Engineers Australia directly or use available resources (guides, FAQs, and contact channels) to reduce errors and delays.

The assessment determines whether your qualifications, knowledge and English proficiency meet Australian standards required for skilled migration and employment in nominated ANZSCO accounting roles.

blocks.x: Overview

CPA Australia is a designated assessing authority for a range of accounting and finance occupations. A positive CPA qualification assessment confirms that your tertiary education and subject coverage are comparable to the Australian standard for your nominated occupation. Where required, a skilled employment assessment can then verify your relevant work experience for migration purposes.
Occupations assessed
Common ANZSCO occupations assessed include:

items.x: Accountant (general) — 221111
Management Accountant — 221112
Taxation Accountant — 221113
External Auditor — 221213
Corporate Treasurer — 221212
Finance Manager — 132211

blocks.x: Choose the ANZSCO code that best reflects your usual duties and qualifications.
Types of assessment

items.x: Qualification assessment — checks degree comparability, coverage of mandatory competencies and English proficiency.
Skilled employment assessment — evaluates your work history and duties; generally requires a suitable qualification assessment outcome first.

blocks.x: Assessment criteria

items.x: Degree comparability: Your primary qualification must be assessed as comparable to at least an Australian bachelor’s degree using Australian government comparability guidelines.

Educational knowledge: The qualification is checked for coverage of mandatory competencies specific to the nominated ANZSCO occupation (e.g., financial accounting and reporting, management accounting, audit and assurance, business law, quantitative methods, Australian taxation law where required). Accredited courses may map competencies automatically.
English proficiency: All applicants must demonstrate the required standard of English (acceptable tests and scores are specified by CPA Australia).

blocks.x: Documents you will need
Prepare certified copies (and accredited translations where needed) of:

items.x: Academic transcripts and degree certificates
Detailed course syllabus or accredited course evidence (if not on CPA’s accredited list)
Identity documents (passport, birth certificate)
CV / resume outlining employment history
Employment references for skilled employment assessment (duties, dates, employer contact details)
Proof of English language test results (if required)

blocks.x: How to apply (overview)

items.x: Identify the CPA occupation/ANZSCO code that best fits your skills.
Check whether your qualification is on CPA Australia’s accredited list (reduces documentary requirements).
Prepare certified documents, translations and English test results.
Submit your application and pay the fee via CPA Australia’s online portal.
Monitor your application and provide any additional information promptly if requested.

blocks.x: Outcome, validity and next steps

If successful, CPA Australia will issue an assessment outcome that states whether your qualification and knowledge are suitable for the nominated occupation. A positive qualification outcome may be required before lodging a visa application or requesting a skilled employment assessment. Check CPA Australia for the validity period of assessment outcomes.
Fees, processing times and support

Fees and processing times vary by assessment type and completeness of documentation. Check CPA Australia’s website for current fees, published processing times and application guidance. Use CPA’s FAQs, checklists and contact channels if you need help; consider a registered migration agent for visa-specific advice.
Important notes & disclaimer

CPA Australia assesses qualifications and employment suitability but does not provide migration advice or award migration points. For visa eligibility, lodgement and points queries contact the Department of Home Affairs or a registered migration agent. Ensure all documents are correctly certified and translated to avoid delays.

seo.description: ANMAC assesses qualifications and practice against Australian migration standards; AHPRA (with the Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia, NMBA) assesses.
seo.h1: Nursing AHPRA Registration and ANMAC Skill Assessment Process

hero.h1: Nursing AHPRA Registration and ANMAC Skill Assessment Process
intro: ANMAC assesses qualifications and practice against Australian migration standards; AHPRA (with the Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia, NMBA) assesses professional registration and competence to practise.

blocks.x: How ANMAC skills assessment works (for migration)

The Australian Nursing & Midwifery Accreditation Council (ANMAC) provides a criteria‑based skills assessment for nurses, midwives and direct care workers applying for a skilled migration visa. ANMAC’s outcome is typically required by the Department of Home Affairs for visa lodgement.

items.x: **Purpose:** confirm your qualifications, registration history and practice are appropriate for migration purposes (ANMAC does not register or license you to work in Australia).
**Who needs it:** internationally qualified nurses, midwives and some direct care workers seeking a skills assessment for skilled migration.

**What ANMAC assesses:**Identity verification and certified ID documents Primary qualification(s) and academic transcripts Work experience and role/duties (employment references) Current/past professional registration and certificates of good standing For full skills assessments, evidence of English language proficiency (ANMAC publishes accepted tests)

**Typical steps:** Create an ANMAC application (online) and choose the correct assessment type. Upload certified supporting documents (ID, qualification certificates and transcripts, proof of registration, employment references, English test results, translations where required). ANMAC reviews documents and may request additional information or verification. Primary source verification may be undertaken. ANMAC issues an outcome (suitable / not suitable). If suitable, you receive an outcome letter to include with visa applications. If you disagree with the result, ANMAC has an appeals/review process (see their appeals policy).

blocks.x: **Documents commonly required:** passport, certified degree certificate(s) and transcripts, detailed employment references (role, duties, dates, hours), registration certificates and letters of good standing from previous regulators, English test result, certified translations.
**Important:** ANMAC outcomes are for migration assessment only — they do not grant registration to practise in Australia.
How AHPRA / NMBA registration works (to practise)
To work as a nurse or midwife in Australia you must be registered with AHPRA under the Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA). Registration is a separate process to ANMAC assessment.

items.x: **Purpose:** determine whether you are competent, fit and suitable to practise in Australia, and allocate the appropriate registration type (e.g., Registered Nurse — Division 1).

**Common applicant pathways for internationally qualified nurses:** Qualification assessed as substantially equivalent: may lead to direct registration (subject to meeting English and other checks). Competency or bridging pathway (where gaps in qualifications/competence are identified): completion of an NMBA‑approved bridging program or Competency Assessment Program (CAP) may be required. Supervised practice: temporary or provisional registration with a period of supervised practice for some applicants.

**What AHPRA/NMBA assesses:**Verified identity and identity documents Primary qualification and evidence of knowledge/competence English language skills (NMBA accepts specific tests — check current NMBA standards for exact tests and score requirements) Criminal history / police checks (international and Australian) Fitness to practise declarations (health/impairment information) Registration status and certificates of good standing from jurisdictions where you were registered

**Typical steps:**Create a myAHPRA account and choose the correct registration pathway and application form. Lodge application with certified documents, registration history and English test evidence. AHPRA/NMBA assesses your application and either: grant registration, request further information, or require completion of a bridging/competency program. If bridging or supervised practice is required, complete the program with an approved education provider or employer and then apply for full registration when requirements are met.

blocks.x: **Important:** registration can take weeks to months depending on pathway and completeness of documentation.
Relationship between ANMAC and AHPRA

items.x: **ANMAC =** migration skills assessment (used for visa purposes). A positive ANMAC outcome does not equal AHPRA registration.
**AHPRA/NMBA =** professional registration to practise in Australia. You must satisfy AHPRA/NMBA requirements even if ANMAC outcome is positive.

**Practical path for many overseas nurses:**Obtain ANMAC skills assessment (if you are migrating). Use ANMAC outcome when lodging visa application with Department of Home Affairs. Separate or subsequent application to AHPRA/NMBA for registration to practise — follow whatever pathway (direct, bridging, supervised) NMBA determines.

blocks.x: Practical checklist (documents & steps)

items.x: **Prepare certified copies of:** Passport (biographical page) Primary nursing/midwifery qualification certificate(s) and full academic transcripts Detailed employment references (duties, start/end dates, hours worked) Current and past registration certificates and letters of good standing Evidence of English language proficiency (results of IELTS, OET, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, etc.) Police/criminal history checks from countries you’ve lived in Any required translations (accredited translator)
**Create accounts and apply online:**ANMAC online application for skills assessment (for migration) myAHPRA online application for registration (for practising)
Monitor emails for requests for further evidence and respond promptly.

blocks.x: Timing, costs and additional notes

items.x: Processing times and fees vary by ANMAC, AHPRA pathway and completeness of your application. Expect several weeks to months.
English test score and acceptable tests may change — always check NMBA/AHPRA and ANMAC official guidance for current requirements.

ANMAC and AHPRA cannot give migration advice — for visa eligibility contact the Department of Home Affairs or a registered migration agent. AHPRA does not place you in employment; employers may require additional checks (immunisation, working with children checks, police checks).
If you are already in Australia on a visa, check any visa conditions that affect study or work while you wait for registration.

blocks.x: Getting help

items.x: Use official ANMAC and AHPRA/NMBA guidance pages and the published document checklists before applying.
Consider contacting approved education providers for bridging programs or using a registered migration agent or immigration lawyer for combined migration + registration strategy.
Keep certified originals and clear copies of each document; track submissions and save receipts and reference numbers.
