seo.description: The Global Talent Independent program is closed. It ended on 6 December 2024. The open visa is the National Innovation visa (subclass 858).

intro: This program is closed. It ended on 6 December 2024. Do not use a Global Talent expression of interest or unique identifier to apply now. The open visa is the [National Innovation visa](/migrate-to-australia/national-innovation-visa-858).

blocks.x: The Global Talent Independent program is closed. The steps further down this page are the old program. They are not how you apply now. The open visa is the [National Innovation visa (subclass 858)](/migrate-to-australia/national-innovation-visa-858). You need a new expression of interest and an invitation.
**Who the program is for**
**The GTI is for people who:**

items.x: Are internationally recognised and prominent in their field (usually for the past two years).
Can demonstrate outstanding achievements (senior roles, awards, publications, patents, high-impact projects).
Can show they will be an asset to Australia and are likely to find work or establish themselves here.
Are able to attract a salary at or above the Fair Work high‑income threshold (the threshold changes yearly; for example it was around $175,000 in recent years).

blocks.x: **Target sectors (examples)**

Resources; Agri‑food & AgTech; Energy; Health industries; Defence, Advanced Manufacturing & Space; Circular economy; DigiTech; Infrastructure & Tourism; Financial services & FinTech; Education. (Specialisations within these sectors include AI, robotics, biotech, precision medicine, quantum computing, renewable energy, AgTech, space tech and more.)
**How to get started (simple steps)**

items.x: Submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) or contact a Global Talent Officer to seek a unique identifier.
Secure a nominator who has national reputation in your field (an Australian citizen/permanent resident, eligible NZ citizen or Australian organisation).
If you receive a unique identifier or an invitation, lodge the visa application with the identifier and required documents.
Wait for health, character and visa checks to be completed and for the visa decision.

blocks.x: **About the unique identifier and nominator**

items.x: Unique identifier: issued to people who meet the program criteria after assessment by Global Talent Officers or via the EOI process.

Nominator: must have a national reputation in the same field and be able to support your application (examples: a university, employer, industry body or recognised leader). The Department checks the nominator’s standing (achievements, leadership, publications, industry roles).

blocks.x: **Two application pathways**

items.x: Global Talent pathway: priority processing after invitation; suitable for candidates in priority sectors.
Distinguished Talent / Legacy pathway: for individuals with truly exceptional international recognition (this pathway can have longer processing times).

blocks.x: **Documents you should prepare**

items.x: Passport and identity documents.
Evidence of international recognition and achievements (awards, publications, patents, contracts, senior role descriptions).
Payslips or job offers showing ability to meet the high‑income threshold, or evidence of recent PhD work in a target sector where applicable.
Nominator’s supporting statement and evidence of their national reputation.
Police checks, health checks and certified English translations where needed.

blocks.x: **Benefits of the program**

items.x: Priority processing in many cases.
No upper age limit for applicants.
Permanent residence if the visa is granted (work, study and possible access to services subject to eligibility).

blocks.x: **Costs and timing (indicative)**

items.x: Visa application fees vary; historic examples include amounts around several thousand dollars for main applicants and lower fees for dependents. Processing times differ by pathway and caseload; Distinguished Talent applications can take much longer than the GTI priority pathway.

blocks.x: **Important cautions**

items.x: Being eligible does not guarantee an invitation or visa — places and invitations are limited and competitive.
Policy and intake details change; check current Home Affairs guidance (including replacement National Innovation visa rules) before applying.
Use an authorised migration professional only after checking official guidance on who can help.

intro: How to Claim Regional Points for Australian Skilled Migration Australia encourages skilled migrants to live and work in regional areas by offering additional points for regional nomination or regio...

These **regional points** can significantly enhance your eligibility for skilled migration visas, helping you achieve your Australian dream.
At **Bansal Immigration**, we specialize in guiding you through the process of claiming regional points effectively and efficiently.
**What Are Regional Points?**

Regional points are part of Australia’s immigration points test. If you live, work, or study in designated regional areas of Australia, you may be eligible to claim additional points, boosting your chances of securing a visa.
**Who Can Claim Regional Points?**
You may be eligible for regional points if you:

items.x: Live and Study in Regional Areas : Completing a course in a designated regional area of Australia.
Work in a Regional Area : Employed in a regional area as part of your visa conditions.
Receive a Regional Sponsorship : Nominated by a state or territory government for living and working in a regional area.

Obtain Regional SponsorshipApply for state or territory nomination under visas such as the 491 Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) Visa or the 190 Skilled Nominated Visa .
Provide EvidenceSubmit necessary documents like course completion certificates, proof of residence, and employment records.

blocks.x: **Benefits of Regional Points**

items.x: Gain 5 to 15 extra points for your visa application.
Increase your chances of receiving an invitation to apply for skilled migration visas.
Access faster visa processing through regional pathways.

Provide Expert Advice : Offer insights into regional opportunities, courses, and jobs.

blocks.x: **Why Choose Regional Australia?**

items.x: Diverse Career Opportunities : Growing industries and less competition.

seo.title: ENS 186 Labour Agreement Stream | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: The subclass 186 Labour Agreement stream is the permanent visa for workers nominated under a labour agreement, including DAMA. Permanent residence is not automatic.

intro: This is a permanent visa. Your employer must have a labour agreement with the Australian Government, and they must nominate you. The agreement sets the job, the age limit, the English level, and the skills you need. It also has to allow permanent residence for your job. A Designated Area Migration Agreement (DAMA) is one type of labour agreement. Getting this visa is not automatic.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: No set time. Check the Department's guide

blocks.x: There are three ways to get a subclass 186 visa. This page is the Labour Agreement stream. The other two are the [Temporary Residence Transition stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-trt) and the [Direct Entry stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-direct). Use this one when your employer has a current labour agreement, and that agreement lets your job lead to permanent residence.

A labour agreement can be a [DAMA](/employer-sponsored/dama), an industry agreement, or an agreement for one company. New [Global Talent Employer Sponsored](/employer-sponsored/gtes) agreements are closed. An old agreement helps only if it is still current and it lists your job.
You cannot apply for this stream on your own. The employer nominates you. You then apply for the visa.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: Your employer is a party to a current labour agreement.
The agreement includes permanent residence for your occupation. If it does not, this stream is not open to you.
You will work for that employer in the nominated position.
You meet the age, English, skills, qualifications and work experience in the agreement. If the agreement does not give a higher age limit, you must be under 45.
Your pay and conditions are at least as good as those for an Australian worker in the same job.
You meet health and character requirements.
Get a skills assessment only if the labour agreement or the Department asks for one.
Permanent residence if the agreement includes that option and the visa is granted.
Occupations that are not on the standard skilled lists, where the agreement lists them.
A higher age limit, an easier English score, or lower pay is allowed only if your agreement says so.
You can include eligible family members.
Once the visa is granted, you can live and work in Australia as a permanent resident. Citizenship has its own rules.
Read the labour agreement for your job. Check that it allows permanent residence. Write down the age, English, skills and pay rules.

If the pathway is a DAMA, start with the [DAMA page](/employer-sponsored/dama), then the [South Australia](/employer-sponsored/dama-south-australia) or [Victoria](/employer-sponsored/dama-victoria) page if that is the region.
The employer lodges a nomination under the Labour Agreement stream.
You lodge the visa application and pay the visa application charge.
Provide evidence that you meet the agreement, plus health and character documents.
Answer any request from the Department, including a skills assessment if one is requested.
If the visa is granted, read the conditions. If you are outside Australia, check the date you must enter by.
**Initial duration.** Permanent.

blocks.x: Australian citizenship after permanent residence

You can apply for [Australian citizenship](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral) after you have lived in Australia for 4 years, including at least 12 months as a permanent resident. You also need to meet the character rules and, in most cases, pass the [citizenship test](/citizenship/citizenship-test). The visa is not guaranteed. Citizenship is a separate application.

If the main applicant does not have functional English, there is a second fee of AUD 9,800 before the visa is granted. Each other applicant aged 18 or over pays AUD 4,890. You do not pay this second fee if you have functional English. The labour agreement may allow a lower English score for the visa. That is separate from this fee. Check the pricing table.
The employer also pays nomination fees and the Skilling Australians Fund levy. These are not part of your visa fee. See the [nomination guide](/employer-sponsored/nomination-process).

**You do not meet the agreement's English, age or salary terms.**
**The endorsement or the nomination** is refused.

**The agreement can expire.** A lodge outside its dates can fail.

faqs.q: Is this the DAMA permanent visa?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Most DAMA pathways use the Labour Agreement stream of subclass 482, 494 or 186. Permanent residence is available only if that agreement includes it for your occupation.

faqs.q: Do I need a skills assessment before I apply?
faqs.a: Only if the labour agreement or the Department asks for one. Do not get one early just because other 186 visas need it. Direct Entry is different.

faqs.q: What is the age limit?
faqs.a: Under 45, unless the labour agreement sets a higher age for your job. Read your agreement. A higher age for another region, or another job, does not apply to you.

seo.description: The Hong Kong stream of subclass 189 is a permanent visa for eligible Hong Kong and British National (Overseas) passport holders. There is no points test and no invitation.
seo.h1: Skilled Independent Visa (189) Hong Kong Stream

hero.h1: Skilled Independent Visa (189) Hong Kong Stream
intro: This is a permanent visa for people who hold a Hong Kong passport or a British National (Overseas) passport. There is no points test and no invitation. You must hold an eligible subclass 457, 482 or 485 visa. You must have lived in Australia as your home for 4 years in a row, right before you apply. A new subclass 457 is closed. The checklist on the main 189 page is only for the points-tested stream.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Check the pricing table. The points-tested stream on our 189 page is AUD 6,135
No set time. Check the Department's guide

blocks.x: This is not the [points-tested subclass 189](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189). You do not need a skills assessment, an expression of interest, or an invitation. You do need the right passport, an eligible temporary visa, and 4 years of living in Australia as your home.

The visas that count are subclass 457, [482](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) and [485](/migrate-to-australia/temporary-graduate-visa-subclass-485). You must be the main visa holder, not a family member on that visa. A new subclass 457 is closed. You can use a 457 only if you still hold one. Home Affairs has extra rules about which visa grant counts, including the date it was granted. Check those rules against your grant letters before you apply.
If you lived in a listed regional area, also read the [191 Hong Kong stream](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-191-hong-kong). That stream looks at 3 years in a regional area.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: You hold a Hong Kong SAR passport or a British National (Overseas) passport.
You hold an eligible subclass 457, 482 or 485 visa, and you are the main visa holder. A new 457 is closed.
You have lived in Australia as your home for at least 4 years in a row, right before you apply.
You have complied with the conditions of that visa.
You meet health and character requirements.
You can show functional English, or you pay a second visa fee if the Department asks for it. This applies to applicants aged 18 or over.
You can include family members. They do not need to meet the 4-year test for the main visa holder. They must meet the health and character rules.
Permanent residence without a points test or an invitation.
No upper age limit on this stream.
After grant, you can live and work anywhere in Australia.
You can later apply for [Australian citizenship](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral) if you meet the residence rules.
Check your passport and your visa grant letters. You must be the main holder of an eligible 457, 482 or 485. A new 457 cannot be used.
Collect proof that Australia was your home for the 4 years before you apply. Use leases, work records, bills and travel records. Short trips are looked at. Long trips away can break the 4 years.
Apply in ImmiAccount. Include identity documents, your visa history, proof you lived here, and health and character documents.
Reply if the Department asks for more information. If an applicant aged 18 or over does not have functional English, allow for the second fee.
If the visa is granted, you become a permanent resident on that date. Citizenship is a later, separate application.
**Initial duration.** Permanent.

blocks.x: Citizenship, and the regional alternative

Citizenship needs 4 years of residence, including 12 months as a permanent resident, plus character requirements and, in most cases, the [citizenship test](/citizenship/citizenship-test). See [citizenship by conferral](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral).

If you do not have 4 years in Australia, but you have 3 years in a listed regional area on an eligible 457, 482 or 485, read the [191 Hong Kong stream](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-191-hong-kong). Check the address on the [postcode checker](/postcode-checker).

If an applicant aged 18 or over does not have functional English, a second fee of AUD 4,885 can apply before the visa is granted. You do not pay it if you have functional English. Check this amount on the pricing table too.

faqs.q: Is there a points test?
faqs.a: No. The Hong Kong stream does not use the points test and does not need an invitation.

faqs.q: Does time on a student visa count?
faqs.a: Time on a student visa can count towards living in Australia. You still must hold an eligible 457, 482 or 485 as the main visa holder. A student visa on its own is not enough.

faqs.q: What if I have spent time outside Australia?
faqs.a: Home Affairs looks at where you actually lived, and whether Australia was your home. Long trips away can affect the 4-year test. Bring your travel records to an appointment before you apply.

seo.h1: Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) Visa (191) Hong Kong Stream

hero.h1: Permanent Residence (Skilled Regional) Visa (191) Hong Kong Stream
intro: This is a permanent visa if you hold a Hong Kong passport or a British National (Overseas) passport, you hold an eligible subclass 457, 482 or 485 visa, and you have lived in a listed regional area for at least 3 years. There is no points test and no invitation. This is not the visa for people who hold a subclass 491 or 494.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Not the AUD 630 regional provisional charge. Check the pricing table
No set time. Check the Department's guide

blocks.x: The [main 191 page](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191) is for people who have held a [491](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491) or a [494](/employer-sponsored/skilled-regional-494) for at least 3 years. You need a Hong Kong or British National (Overseas) passport. You must be the main holder of an eligible 457, 482 or 485. You must have lived in a listed regional area as your home for at least 3 years in a row, right before you apply. The income test and the tax notices are for the 491 and 494 stream. They are not the test for this Hong Kong stream.

You hold an eligible subclass 457, 482 or 485 visa as the main visa holder. A new 457 is closed.

You meet health and character requirements.

Permanent residence without a points test, an invitation or an employer nomination.
No upper age limit on this stream.
Once the visa is granted, you can live and work anywhere in Australia. The regional rule is only for the 3 years before the visa is granted.
Eligible family members can be included.

Apply in ImmiAccount. Include your identity documents, passport, visa history, proof you lived in a regional area, and health and character documents.
If the visa is granted, you can live anywhere in Australia. Citizenship is a separate application.
**Initial duration.** Permanent.

After the visa is granted, [citizenship](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral) needs 4 years in Australia, including 12 months as a permanent resident. You also need to meet the character rules and, in most cases, pass the [citizenship test](/citizenship/citizenship-test).

seo.title: Australian Citizenship for New Zealand Citizens (Subclass 444) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: Eligible New Zealand citizens on a Special Category visa (subclass 444) can apply for Australian citizenship without first getting a permanent visa. The 189 New Zealand stream is closed.
seo.h1: Australian Citizenship for New Zealand Citizens on a Subclass 444 Visa

hero.h1: Australian Citizenship for New Zealand Citizens on a Subclass 444 Visa
intro: From 1 July 2023, an eligible New Zealand citizen on a Special Category visa (subclass 444) can apply for Australian citizenship without first getting another permanent visa. The New Zealand stream of subclass 189 is closed to new applications. Time on a 444 can count towards the time you need in Australia.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Citizenship by conferral, not a permanent visa
4 years lawful residence, with the last 12 months counted as permanent residence

blocks.x: A New Zealand citizen is usually given a [Special Category visa (subclass 444)](/transit-special-purpose/special-category-visa-444) when they arrive. You can live and work in Australia. The 444 is still a temporary visa. It ends when you leave Australia. It can be given again when you return, if you still qualify.

For citizenship, you are usually treated as a permanent resident from 1 July 2022 if you held a subclass 444 before that date. If your first 444 was on or after 1 July 2022, the date is the day that visa was granted. You need this date for the rule that you must be a permanent resident for the last 12 months.
The [points-tested subclass 189](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189) is a different visa. Its New Zealand stream is closed. Do not apply for it.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: You are a New Zealand citizen. You hold a subclass 444 when you apply, and you still hold it when a decision is made.
You have lived in Australia lawfully for 4 years immediately before you apply.
You meet the permanent residence part of the test. For an eligible 444 holder, use the start date explained above.
You were outside Australia for no more than 12 months in total in those 4 years, and for no more than 90 days in the last 12 months.
You meet the identity and character requirements, including police checks.
You pass the [citizenship test](/citizenship/citizenship-test) if you need to. Some people do not have to sit it.
You plan to live in Australia, or to keep a close and continuing link with Australia.
You do not need a skilled visa or an employer-sponsored permanent visa first.

Once citizenship is granted, you are an Australian citizen. See [dual citizenship](/citizenship/dual-citizenship). New Zealand lets its citizens hold another citizenship. Check your own situation before you apply.

A child born in Australia on or after 1 July 2022 to a subclass 444 holder may already be an Australian citizen. Read the note on the [subclass 444 page](/transit-special-purpose/special-category-visa-444) and [citizenship by birth](/citizenship/citizenship-by-birth).
Confirm you hold a subclass 444 and work out your permanent residence start date for citizenship.
Count your absences. Use travel records, not memory.
Read [citizenship by conferral](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral) for the usual steps, then send the citizenship application.
Get police checks for Australia and for other countries where you lived for the time Home Affairs asks for.
Sit the citizenship test if you are required to.
If approved, attend the citizenship ceremony.
**This is not a visa application.** Citizenship does not expire. The subclass 444 still ends each time you leave Australia, until you become a citizen or hold another visa.

blocks.x: Family members who are not New Zealand citizens

A partner or child who is not a New Zealand citizen does not get a subclass 444. They need their own visa. The usual one is the [New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship visa (subclass 461)](/family-visa/new-zealand-citizen-family-relationship-visa-subclass-461). A partner of an Australian citizen or permanent resident should look at the [partner visas](/family-visa).

Citizenship applications do not use the visa processing times guide. Home Affairs publishes a separate time for citizenship. Check that time before you apply. It is a guide, not a promise for your application.
Citizenship has its own fee. It is not a visa fee. Check the amount on the Home Affairs citizenship page before you apply. The fee can change with how you apply, and some people pay less.

items.x: [Special Category visa (444)](/transit-special-purpose/special-category-visa-444)
[Citizenship by conferral](/citizenship/citizenship-by-conferral)
[Citizenship test](/citizenship/citizenship-test)
[Citizenship by birth](/citizenship/citizenship-by-birth)
[Dual citizenship](/citizenship/dual-citizenship)
[New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship visa (461)](/family-visa/new-zealand-citizen-family-relationship-visa-subclass-461)

faqs.q: Do I still need permanent residence first?
faqs.a: You do not need a separate permanent visa, such as a 189 or 186. From 1 July 2023, an eligible subclass 444 holder is treated as a permanent resident for the citizenship time test, from the start date on this page.

faqs.q: What happened to the 189 New Zealand stream?
faqs.a: It is closed to new applications. For eligible New Zealand citizens, the citizenship option on this page replaced it.

faqs.q: Can my partner who is not a New Zealand citizen apply with me?
faqs.a: No. They need their own visa, often a subclass 461, and their own citizenship application later if they become eligible.

seo.title: South Australia DAMA | Adelaide and Regional SA | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: South Australia has two Designated Area Migration Agreements: one for Adelaide technology and innovation, and one for the regional workforce across the state. An employer must sponsor you.
seo.h1: Designated Area Migration Agreements in South Australia

hero.h1: Designated Area Migration Agreements in South Australia
intro: South Australia has two DAMAs. The Adelaide agreement covers technology, defence, space, advanced manufacturing and innovation in greater Adelaide. The regional agreement covers the state, including farming, health, aged care, tourism, hospitality, construction and trades. You cannot apply on your own. An employer in the area must sponsor you.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: An employer endorsed for the relevant South Australian DAMA
Labour Agreement stream of subclass 482, 494 or 186
The charge for the visa in the agreement. Subclass 482 base charge is AUD 4,015
Only if that agreement includes it for the occupation

blocks.x: Read the [DAMA overview](/employer-sponsored/dama) first. A DAMA is an agreement between the Australian Government and a regional body. It can list jobs that are not on the usual skilled lists. For some jobs it can allow a higher age, an easier English score, or lower pay. That easier rule is written next to the job. It is not a discount for every job.
**Adelaide City Technology and Innovation Advancement DAMA.** This is for greater Adelaide and for the technology and innovation occupations in that agreement.
**South Australian Regional Workforce DAMA.** This is for employers across South Australia in the industries that agreement covers.
This is not the same as [South Australian state nomination](/south-australia-state-nomination) for a subclass 190 or 491. State nomination does not need this employer agreement. A DAMA does.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: The job is in the area covered by that agreement, and the job is on that agreement's current list.
The South Australian office that runs the DAMA approves the employer. The employer then signs a labour agreement with the Department of Home Affairs.

You meet the age, English, skills, experience and pay in the agreement for that job. Do not assume an easier rule applies. Many lists give a lower English score, or pay below the usual amount, only for named jobs.

The visa is the Labour Agreement stream of the [482](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482), the [494](/employer-sponsored/skilled-regional-494), or the [186](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement). The agreement says which one you can use.
You meet health and character requirements.
Occupations that standard sponsorship does not cover, where the SA list includes them.
Easier rules apply only where the job line says so. Some DAMAs allow an age over 45. Easier English and lower pay also depend on the job.

A path to permanent residence through the [186 Labour Agreement stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement), if the agreement includes it. This is often after you have worked on a 482 or 494 from the same agreement.
Our Adelaide office can help the employer and the worker. Adelaide: Unit 5, 55 Gawler Place. Phone +61 8 8317 1340.

The employer checks the current South Australian job list, and the end date of the agreement, with Skilled and Business Migration in South Australia. Lists and end dates change. Do not use an old PDF.
The employer seeks endorsement from the Designated Area Representative.
The employer signs the labour agreement with the Department of Home Affairs.
The employer nominates the worker. See the [nomination guide](/employer-sponsored/nomination-process).
The worker lodges the 482, 494 or 186 visa named in the nomination.
**482 under a DAMA.** Temporary. The visa grant sets how long you can stay. A standard 482 is up to 4 years.
**494 under a DAMA.** Provisional, usually 5 years, and tied to regional Australia.
**186 under a DAMA.** Permanent, if the agreement allows that nomination and the visa is granted.

blocks.x: Permanent residence

There is no separate DAMA permanent visa. The permanent visa is the [186 Labour Agreement stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement). Some workers hold a [494](/employer-sponsored/skilled-regional-494) and later look at subclass [191](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191). The open option depends on the visa you hold and on the agreement. Permanent residence is not automatic.

head: Type
Time
rows: Check the [Home Affairs guide](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-processing-times). It shows recent decisions. It is not a promise for your application.

blocks.x: A DAMA has no visa fee of its own. You pay the fee for the visa in the agreement. The subclass 482 base fee is AUD 4,015. The subclass 494 and subclass 186 base fee on those pages is AUD 6,140.

These amounts are from the Department of Home Affairs [current visa pricing table](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing). Charges can change. Check the table before you apply. Some citizens of Pacific Island countries, Timor-Leste and ASEAN countries pay less for some visas.
The employer also pays approval, nomination and levy costs. Ask what these are before the employer requests the agreement.

faqs.q: Is Adelaide covered?
faqs.a: Greater Adelaide is covered by the Adelaide technology and innovation DAMA, for the jobs on that list. The regional workforce DAMA covers more jobs across South Australia. Check which agreement lists the job.

faqs.q: Can I apply without an employer?
faqs.a: No. An endorsed employer must sponsor and nominate you.

faqs.q: Is the salary always 90 per cent of the threshold?
faqs.a: No. Lower pay is allowed only if the agreement says so for that job. The pay must still meet the rate in the agreement, and the going rate where that is required.

seo.description: DAMA options for employers in the Goulburn Valley and the Great South Coast. Melbourne is not a DAMA area. An employer must sponsor the worker.
seo.h1: Designated Area Migration Agreements in Victoria

hero.h1: Designated Area Migration Agreements in Victoria
intro: This page covers two Victorian DAMAs: the Goulburn Valley DAMA and the Great South Coast DAMA. Approved employers in those regions can sponsor workers for jobs on the agreement list. Some jobs have easier rules. Melbourne is not covered. You cannot apply without an employer.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Goulburn Valley and Great South Coast
Melbourne and other areas that are outside the agreement
Labour Agreement stream of subclass 482, 494 or 186
Only if that agreement includes it for the occupation

blocks.x: Start with the [DAMA overview](/employer-sponsored/dama). Each Victorian agreement has its own local office, job list, postcodes and end date. Check the current list before the employer pays to be approved.

**Goulburn Valley** includes the Shepparton area. **Great South Coast** includes the Warrnambool area. The exact postcodes are in the agreement. Use the [postcode checker](/postcode-checker) only as a guide, then check the address with the local DAMA office. Other parts of Victoria may have their own agreement. This page only covers the two agreements named here.
If the employer is in Melbourne, use a standard [482](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) or [186](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-direct) pathway, not a DAMA.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: The job is in the area covered by the agreement, and it is on that area's current DAMA list.
The local Victorian DAMA office approves the employer. The employer then signs a labour agreement with the Department.
You meet the rules the agreement sets for the job, including any easier rules. Easier rules are not automatic.

The employer nominates you for the Labour Agreement stream of a [482](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482), [494](/employer-sponsored/skilled-regional-494) or [186](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement).
You meet health and character requirements.
Jobs agreed for that region, including jobs that are hard to fill locally.
Age, English and experience concessions where the occupation line provides them.
A path to permanent residence through the [186 Labour Agreement stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement), if the agreement includes it.
Check that the workplace postcode is inside the Goulburn Valley or Great South Coast agreement.
The employer applies for endorsement from that region's Designated Area Representative.
The labour agreement is signed with the Department of Home Affairs.
The employer nominates the worker. See the [nomination guide](/employer-sponsored/nomination-process).
The worker lodges the visa named in the nomination.
**482.** Temporary, up to 4 years on a standard grant.
**494.** Provisional, usually 5 years in regional Australia.
**186.** Permanent, if the agreement allows that nomination and the visa is granted.

blocks.x: Permanent residence

The permanent visa under these agreements is the [186 Labour Agreement stream](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-labour-agreement). A worker on a 494 may later qualify for subclass [191](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191). Check which visa the agreement will use before you start.
South Australian employers should use the [South Australia DAMA page](/employer-sponsored/dama-south-australia).

head: Type
Time
rows: Check the [Home Affairs guide](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-processing-times). It shows recent decisions. It is not a promise for your application.

blocks.x: You pay the visa fee for the subclass in the agreement. The subclass 482 base fee is AUD 4,015. The subclass 494 and subclass 186 base fee on those pages is AUD 6,140.

These amounts are from the Department of Home Affairs [current visa pricing table](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing). Charges can change. Check the table before you apply. Some citizens of Pacific Island countries, Timor-Leste and ASEAN countries pay less for some visas.

faqs.q: Which parts of Victoria are covered here?
faqs.a: The Goulburn Valley DAMA and the Great South Coast DAMA. Check the workplace postcode with the local DAMA office. Do not assume a nearby town is included.

faqs.q: Is Melbourne covered?
faqs.a: No. Employers in Melbourne use the standard employer sponsored visas.

faqs.q: Is there a pathway to permanent residence?
faqs.a: Yes, if the agreement includes the 186 Labour Agreement stream for that job. This is usually after you have worked for a set time. It is not automatic.

seo.title: PALM Scheme Visa (Subclass 403) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: The Pacific Australia Labour Mobility scheme uses the subclass 403 visa. Workers from participating Pacific countries and Timor-Leste need an approved PALM employer. You cannot apply on your own.
seo.h1: Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) Scheme, Subclass 403

hero.h1: Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) Scheme, Subclass 403
intro: The PALM scheme lets approved Australian employers hire workers from listed Pacific island countries and Timor-Leste when they cannot fill the jobs locally. The visa is the PALM stream of the [Temporary Work (International Relations) visa (subclass 403)](/employer-sponsored/temporary-work-international-relations-403). You must be chosen through the government office in your home country that sends workers. You cannot apply on your own with a private job offer.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Citizens of participating Pacific countries and Timor-Leste
Short-term placements up to 9 months, or long-term placements of 1 to 4 years

blocks.x: The countries are Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu. The worker is chosen by the government office in their home country that sends workers, and is employed by an approved PALM employer.

This scheme replaced the Seasonal Worker Programme and the Pacific Labour Scheme. Short-term work is seasonal. Long-term work is from 1 to 4 years. The visa grant and your work agreement set the exact stay.
This is not a [Skills in Demand (482)](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) visa. If an Australian business wants to sponsor a skilled worker outside PALM, use the 482 page.

sections.name: Eligibility
sections.h2: Do You Have What It Takes?

items.x: You are a citizen of a listed country, and you are chosen through that country's office that sends workers.
You are aged 21 or over.
You have a job with an approved PALM scheme employer.
The employer is approved for PALM and can sponsor the subclass 403.
You meet health, character and health insurance requirements.
You apply online as part of that recruitment. An application without that government office will not be accepted.
You can work lawfully in Australia for the approved employer, for the season or for the longer job in your contract.
Short-term workers can return in later seasons where the visa and the scheme allow it.
You can travel in and out of Australia while the visa and the work agreement are valid. You must follow the conditions on the grant.
The employer is approved as a PALM scheme employer. The Department of Employment and Workplace Relations gives that approval. The employer also needs to be able to sponsor the 403.
Hiring goes through the government office in the worker's country. The worker does not arrange a private nomination.
The worker applies online for the subclass 403 PALM stream, with the recruitment papers.
After the visa is granted, the worker works only for the approved employer and follows the visa conditions.
**Short-term.** Up to 9 months in any 12 months. The visa can let you come back each season.
**Long-term.** Between 1 and 4 years, as set in the placement.

blocks.x: There is no PALM permanent visa

The subclass 403 does not lead to permanent residence. Many PALM visas have a no-further-stay condition. That can stop you applying for another visa while you are in Australia, unless the condition is lifted. Read the [403 page](/employer-sponsored/temporary-work-international-relations-403) and your grant letter. A later [482](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) or family visa is a new application with its own rules.

head: Type
Time
rows: Check the [Home Affairs guide](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-processing-times). It shows recent decisions. It is not a promise for your application.

blocks.x: The [403 page](/employer-sponsored/temporary-work-international-relations-403) does not set a dollar amount, because the fee depends on the stream. Check the current visa pricing table for the PALM stream before anyone pays.

These amounts are from the Department of Home Affairs [current visa pricing table](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing). Charges can change. Check the table before you apply. Some citizens of Pacific Island countries, Timor-Leste and ASEAN countries pay less for some visas.

items.x: [Temporary Work (International Relations) 403](/employer-sponsored/temporary-work-international-relations-403)
[Skills in Demand (482)](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482)
[482 Core Skills stream](/employer-sponsored/sid-482-core-skills)
[Short Stay Specialist (400)](/employer-sponsored/short-stay-400)
[Temporary Activity (408)](/employer-sponsored/temporary-activity-408)
[Employer sponsored visas](/employer-sponsored)

faqs.q: Can I apply for this visa myself?
faqs.a: No. You must be chosen through your country's office that sends workers, and sponsored by an approved PALM employer.

faqs.q: Can the job be in a city?
faqs.a: PALM jobs are mainly in regional and rural Australia. Farming and some food processing can be in more places. The employer's PALM approval says where the work can be.

faqs.q: Can I stay and apply for permanent residence?
faqs.a: Not on this visa. There is no direct path to permanent residence. A no-further-stay condition may also stop another application in Australia.

seo.title: Skills assessment for teachers (AITSL) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: How the AITSL skills assessment works for school teachers migrating to Australia: qualifications, supervised teaching, English, and what to do next.

hero.badge: AITSL
intro: If you want to migrate as a school teacher, the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership (AITSL) checks your qualifications and your English. A suitable outcome is what you use for a skilled visa. It does not register you to teach in a classroom.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: University study, initial teacher education, supervised teaching practice, and English
Academic IELTS at a test centre only, if you do not meet the study option

blocks.x: AITSL is the skills assessing authority for these school teacher occupations. Pick the occupation that matches your qualification and the age group you trained to teach. Each occupation has its own checklist.

items.x: **Primary school teacher.** ANZSCO 241213. Supervised practice is with students aged about 5 to 12 in a primary school.
**Middle school teacher.** ANZSCO 241311. For teachers trained for the middle years of schooling.
**Secondary school teacher.** ANZSCO 241411. Supervised practice is with students aged about 13 to 18 in a secondary school.

**Special needs and special education teachers.** Includes Special Needs Teacher (241511), Teacher of the Hearing Impaired (241512), Teacher of the Sight Impaired (241513) and Special Education Teachers nec (241599). The checklist sets the setting and age range for your supervised practice.

blocks.x: Early childhood (pre-primary school) teachers are assessed by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA), not AITSL. That change started on 7 December 2024. An AITSL letter you already hold stays valid until its expiry date.
AITSL looks at two things. You must meet both. A degree on its own is not enough if the teacher-education part, the supervised practice, or the English evidence is missing.

items.x: **Four years of university study.** At least four years full-time, or the part-time equivalent, of higher education that leads to a qualification. This must include a relevant initial teacher education qualification. Other study that counts toward the four years should be at least Australian Advanced Diploma or Associate Degree level (AQF level 6).

**Initial teacher education.** The teacher qualification must be comparable to an Australian bachelor degree (AQF level 7) or higher. It must include at least one year of study in initial teacher education for that occupation, and at least 45 days of supervised teaching practice in the right school setting. Short courses, professional development and unfinished qualifications are not assessed.

**English by study, or by IELTS.** You can meet English with at least four full years of university study in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States, including a recognised initial teacher education qualification. All parts of that teacher qualification, including the supervised practice, must have been done in one or more of those countries.

**Or Academic IELTS.** If you use a test, AITSL accepts only Academic IELTS done at a test centre, on paper or on computer. You need at least 7.0 in Reading and Writing, and at least 8.0 in Speaking and Listening, on one Test Report Form, from a test in the last three years. AITSL accepts IELTS One Skill Retake. It does not accept PTE, TOEFL, Cambridge, IELTS Online or IELTS Indicator.

blocks.x: AITSL can still ask you to sit Academic IELTS if it is not sure about your English, even if you have claimed the study option. Read the occupation checklist before you apply, and see our [skills assessment guide](/skill-assessment/guide) for how a skills assessment fits into a visa.

sections.name: Assessment and registration
sections.h2: A skills assessment is not teacher registration

blocks.x: A suitable AITSL outcome tells the Department of Home Affairs that your qualifications and English meet the standard for the nominated occupation. The teacher registration authority in the state or territory decides whether you can teach in a school. In Victoria that is the Victorian Institute of Teaching. You may need both: AITSL for the visa, and registration before you teach.

The same split applies in other professions. Nurses use a migration assessment and a separate registration. See [nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment). Doctors use Medical Board registration as the skills assessment. Read [skills assessment for doctors](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-doctors).

why.title: Check the visa needs it
why.desc: Confirm with Home Affairs, or with us, that the visa you want asks for a skills assessment in this occupation.

why.title: Match the occupation
why.desc: Your qualification, the age group and the school setting should match the AITSL checklist you choose.

why.title: Gather the evidence
why.desc: You will need identity documents, qualification certificates, full transcripts, proof of supervised teaching practice, and English evidence.

steps.title: Apply online to AITSL
steps.desc: Upload a complete application. Missing or wrong documents slow it down.

steps.title: Wait for the outcome
steps.desc: AITSL says most complete applications are finished within about four weeks, and some take up to six. It does not give status updates by phone or email.

steps.title: Use the letter in your visa
steps.desc: A suitable outcome can go into an Expression of Interest and, if you are invited, the visa application. It does not guarantee an invitation or a visa grant.

blocks.x: Fees change. AITSL published a new fee structure from 7 September 2026. Check the AITSL website for the current fee before you apply. For how long assessments usually take across authorities, see the [assessment timeline](/skill-assessment/timeline).

A positive skills assessment is one part of [how skilled migration works](/migrate-to-australia). You still need the occupation on the right list, enough points, and an invitation or a sponsor. Teachers are often invited through a state or territory.

items.x: **Skilled Independent (subclass 189).** No sponsor. You need an invitation. See the [189 visa](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189).
**Skilled Nominated (subclass 190).** A state or territory nominates you. See the [190 visa](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190).
**Skilled Work Regional (subclass 491).** A regional nomination. See the [491 visa](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491).

**A job with an Australian employer.** Some teachers use a [Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) or, later, an [Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186)](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-direct). The skills assessment rules can differ from the points-tested visas.

blocks.x: You can estimate a points score with the [PR points calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator). Points for work and English are separate from the AITSL outcome.

items.x: [Skills assessment for doctors](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-doctors) Medical Board registration as the skills assessment.
[Skills assessment for social workers](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-social-workers) AASW assessment for social workers.
[Nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment) Migration assessment and registration for nurses.
[Skill assessment overview](/skill-assessment) All assessing authorities we help with.
[Skills assessment guide](/skill-assessment/guide) How a skills assessment fits a visa application.
[Skilled migration](/migrate-to-australia) Compare the 189, 190 and 491 visas.

faqs.q: Does a suitable AITSL assessment let me teach in Australia?
faqs.a: No. It is for migration. You still need registration with the teacher registration authority in the state or territory where you want to teach.

faqs.q: Can I use PTE or TOEFL for AITSL?
faqs.a: No. If you use a test, AITSL accepts Academic IELTS at a test centre only. The scores are 7.0 for Reading and Writing, and 8.0 for Speaking and Listening, on one report from the last three years.

faqs.q: I am an early childhood teacher. Do I apply to AITSL?
faqs.a: No. ACECQA assesses Early Childhood (Pre-primary School) Teacher applications lodged from 7 December 2024. AITSL assesses school teacher occupations such as primary, middle, secondary and special education.

faqs.q: How long does AITSL take?
faqs.a: AITSL says most complete applications are finished within about four weeks, and some take up to six weeks. Incomplete documents take longer. AITSL does not answer status requests by phone.

/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-.name: Skills assessment for doctors
keywords: Medical Board of Australia skills assessment

seo.title: Skills assessment for doctors | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: How overseas doctors get a skills assessment for Australian migration through Medical Board registration, and which visa that registration can support.

hero.badge: Medical Board of Australia
intro: For medical practitioners, the skills assessing authority is the Medical Board of Australia. Home Affairs generally treats your registration, issued through Ahpra, as the skills assessment. The type of registration that counts depends on the visa.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Usually general or specialist registration when you are invited
Limited or provisional registration may be accepted on some visas
A visa, or a job offer

blocks.x: Doctors do not send a file to a separate migration assessing body in the way teachers send one to AITSL, or social workers send one to the AASW. The Medical Board of Australia is the assessing authority. The Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) runs the registration application for the Board.

You cannot practise medicine in Australia until the Medical Board registers you. A skills assessment for a visa and the right to practise are tied together. Compare that with nurses, who need an ANMAC assessment for many visas and a separate Ahpra registration to work. See [nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment).

The Australian Medical Council (AMC) exams are part of the standard pathway to registration. Passing an AMC exam is not, by itself, the visa skills assessment. Home Affairs looks at your Medical Board registration.

International medical graduates use a pathway set by the Medical Board. The right one depends on where you qualified, where you have worked, and whether you are a specialist. Your qualifications must also be checked through primary source verification before registration.

items.x: **Competent Authority pathway.** For doctors who have been assessed by a recognised competent authority and have practised in a competent authority country. It leads toward general registration, usually after supervised practice in Australia.

**Standard pathway.** For doctors who are assessed by the Australian Medical Council. This is usually a written exam first, then a clinical exam or a workplace-based assessment, then registration with a period of supervision.

**Specialist pathway.** A specialist medical college compares your specialist training with Australian training. Many doctors then complete a period of supervised practice before specialist registration. Some specialists can use a faster college pathway and apply for specialist registration more directly.

blocks.x: Which pathway you use changes when you can lodge a points-tested visa. Doctors on the standard, competent authority or specialist pathway often need to finish supervised practice in Australia before they hold general or specialist registration. That registration is what an independent skilled visa usually asks for.

sections.name: Which registration a visa needs
sections.h2: Which registration a visa may accept

blocks.x: Do not assume every visa accepts the same registration. Check the visa you want before you plan around limited registration.

items.x: **Points-tested visas.** For a [subclass 189](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189), [subclass 190](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190) or [subclass 491](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491), Home Affairs usually wants general registration, or specialist registration that lets you practise in your specialty without further training or supervision. You normally need that registration when you are invited.

**Employer-sponsored visas.** A [Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482) or an [Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186)](/employer-sponsored/ens-186-direct) may accept limited or provisional registration in some cases. The employer nominates the position. Not every employer can sponsor, and not every offer leads to a visa.
**You still need a visa that lets you work.** Registration does not give you a visa. If you are already in Australia, check your visa conditions before you start work or a supervised placement.

sections.name: How we help
sections.h2: How we help doctors plan this

why.title: Occupation and list
why.desc: General practitioner, resident medical officer and specialist roles are not the same occupation. The list and the assessing authority have to match the visa.

why.title: Registration type
why.desc: We check whether the registration you can get now is enough for the visa, or whether you need general or specialist registration first.

why.title: Timing
why.desc: AMC exams, college assessment and supervised practice can take a long time. The visa plan should follow that, not the other way around.

steps.title: Confirm the pathway
steps.desc: Use the Medical Board's information for international medical graduates and the college, if you are a specialist.

steps.title: Apply for registration
steps.desc: Lodge with Ahpra when your pathway, exams and primary source verification are ready.

steps.title: Then the visa
steps.desc: Use the registration as the skills assessment in the Expression of Interest, nomination or visa application. See [how skilled migration works](/migrate-to-australia).

items.x: [Skills assessment for teachers (AITSL)](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-teachers) Qualifications and English for school teachers.
[Skills assessment for social workers](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-social-workers) AASW assessment for social workers.
[Nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment) A different health pathway: assessment and registration are separate.
[Skill assessment overview](/skill-assessment) All assessing authorities we help with.
[Assessment requirements](/skill-assessment/requirements) Documents authorities usually ask for.
[PR points calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator) Estimate a points score once you know your occupation.

faqs.q: Is the AMC exam my skills assessment?
faqs.a: No. AMC exams are a step on the standard pathway to registration. For migration, the Medical Board of Australia is the assessing authority, and Home Affairs generally accepts your registration as the skills assessment.

faqs.q: Can I apply for a 189 visa with provisional or limited registration?
faqs.a: Usually no. Independent skilled visas generally need general or specialist registration at the time of invitation. Some employer-sponsored visas can accept limited or provisional registration. Check the visa before you lodge.

faqs.q: Do I need a skills assessment and Ahpra registration?
faqs.a: For doctors they are the same process. The Medical Board registers you through Ahpra, and that registration is what the visa uses as the skills assessment.

faqs.q: I am a nurse, not a doctor. Is this the right page?
faqs.a: No. Nurses and midwives are assessed for migration by ANMAC, and they register with Ahpra under the Nursing and Midwifery Board. Start with [nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment).

seo.title: Skills assessment for social workers | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: How the AASW skills assessment works for social workers migrating to Australia, including qualifications, placements and English.

hero.badge: AASW
intro: The Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) is the assessing authority for the occupation Social Worker. It checks whether your qualification, field placements and English meet the Australian standard for migration.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: A completed social work qualification comparable to an AASW-accredited degree
At least 1,000 hours across at least two placements, for an international qualification
IELTS Academic at a test centre. AASW does not accept other tests

blocks.x: You need to be a qualified social worker. The AASW does not assess community services, counselling, psychology or welfare qualifications as social work. If your degree is in another field, a different body may assess that occupation.

items.x: **Overseas social work degree.** Most applicants use the international qualification assessment. The AASW compares your course with an Australian social work degree it accredits.

**Australian graduates.** If you finished an AASW-accredited social work course in Australia, there is a separate application, including one that can support a [Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485)](/migrate-to-australia/temporary-graduate-visa-subclass-485).
**New Zealand qualifications.** Social workers covered by the New Zealand mutual recognition agreement use that AASW application, not the overseas qualification pathway.

**You must have finished the course.** The AASW can start once you have a graduation certificate, or a letter from the university confirming you have completed every course requirement, with your transcript.

blocks.x: Social work is not a profession registered by Ahpra. Doctors and nurses use Ahpra. Social workers use the AASW. If you are a doctor, read [skills assessment for doctors](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-doctors).

The AASW looks at the content of the degree, not only the title on the certificate. For an international qualification it uses published criteria. Those criteria change, so use the guide for your application type.

items.x: **The qualification itself.** It should be a social work qualification at a level the AASW can compare with an accredited Australian bachelor or qualifying master degree. A doctorate in social work has its own application.

**Field placements.** The AASW expects at least 1,000 hours of field education across at least two placements. This was increased from 980 hours so it matches an accredited Australian social work course. You need evidence of the agencies, hours, supervision and the work you did.

**English.** The AASW sets its own English standard for social work practice. It can be higher than the English level Home Affairs uses for a visa. Meeting a visa English score does not mean you meet the AASW score.

blocks.x: The AASW accepts IELTS Academic done face to face at an official test centre, on paper or on computer. It does not accept IELTS Online, PTE, TOEFL or other tests. From 20 May 2026 it can accept an IELTS Academic One Skill Retake in the cases below.

items.x: **One sitting.** At least 7.0 in Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking.

**Two sittings.** You can combine two Academic tests within six months. Each component must reach 7.0 across the two tests, and no component score can be below 6.5. A score under 6.5 makes that test unusable.

**One Skill Retake.** Three components on the original computer-based test are at least 7.0, and the weak component is at least 6.5. You retake that one skill within 60 days and score at least 7.0. The AASW asks that this result be within 12 months of the application.

**Study exemption.** You may not need a test if you finished secondary school in English in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, South Africa, the United Kingdom or the United States, and you also completed at least three years full-time of a bachelor degree or higher, taught and assessed in English, in one of those countries. The AASW can still ask for IELTS if the evidence is not clear.

blocks.x: Keep the test type straight. Teachers applying to AITSL need higher Speaking and Listening scores, and their study exemption is different. See [skills assessment for teachers](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-teachers).

You apply online through a MyAASW account. For the online application, the AASW asks for colour scans of the original documents. They do not need to be certified for that online lodgement. Pay by card at the end. Fees depend on the application type and are listed on the AASW page for that application.

Processing time depends on the application. The AASW emails the outcome and shows status in your account. It does not usually give progress updates by phone. An employer can ask for priority in limited cases. The AASW decides that request. It will not lower the criteria to fit a visa deadline.

A suitable outcome lets you claim the occupation in a skilled visa, such as the [189](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-independent-visa-subclass-189), [190](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190) or [491](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491). It does not grant the visa. If an employer is sponsoring you, look at the [Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)](/employer-sponsored/sid-visa-482). Read [how skilled migration works](/migrate-to-australia) and check your score with the [PR points calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator).

items.x: [Skills assessment for teachers (AITSL)](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-teachers) School teacher qualifications and English.
[Skills assessment for doctors](/skill-assessment/skills-assessment-for-doctors) Medical Board registration for doctors.
[Nursing: AHPRA and ANMAC](/skill-assessment/nursing-aphara-registration-and-anmac-skill-assessment) Another caring profession with a different authority.
[Skill assessment overview](/skill-assessment) All assessing authorities we help with.
[Skills assessment guide](/skill-assessment/guide) Where the assessment sits in a visa application.
[Assessment timeline](/skill-assessment/timeline) How long skills assessments can take.

faqs.q: Can I apply with a community work or counselling degree?
faqs.a: No. The AASW assesses social work qualifications. A different professional body assesses community workers and psychologists. The occupation on your visa must match the qualification.

faqs.q: Is PTE accepted for the AASW assessment?
faqs.a: No. The AASW accepts IELTS Academic at a test centre only. You need 7.0 in each component, in one sitting or across two sittings in six months with no score below 6.5. A qualifying One Skill Retake can be used from 20 May 2026.

faqs.q: Does a positive AASW assessment give me a visa?
faqs.a: No. It shows your qualification is suitable for the occupation. You still need to meet the visa rules, including points or an employer, English for the visa, and an invitation or nomination where that applies.

faqs.q: I studied social work in Australia. Do I use the same form?
faqs.a: Not always. Graduates of an AASW-accredited Australian course, including people applying for a subclass 485 visa, use the application for that pathway. Check the AASW guide before you pay.

intro: Western Australia nominates for the 190 and 491 visas. There is no separate Registration of Interest. WA invites people from SkillSelect.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: AUD 200, non-refundable, when you lodge the nomination application.
People already living in WA, then priority industries, then higher points.

blocks.x: Select Western Australia in your Expression of Interest. Your occupation must be on the list for the stream and the visa you want. A provisional skills assessment issued for a subclass 485 visa is not accepted.

WA ranks people living in Western Australia ahead of people interstate or overseas. Priority industries are building and construction, health care and social assistance, hospitality and tourism, and education and training.

If your EOI asks for both a 190 and a 491, WA will usually invite you for the 491 first, because that score is higher. You can lodge only one nomination application. If an invitation lapses, you need a new EOI.

blocks.x: General stream

Occupations are on WASMOL Schedule 1 or Schedule 2. Schedule 1 usually needs at least one year of Australian or overseas work in the nominated or closely related occupation in the last 10 years. For a subclass 190 in Schedule 1, you usually also need a full-time WA employment contract of at least six months. Some building and construction occupations are exempt. Schedule 2 does not use that same contract test. Read the schedule that lists your occupation.
Defence industry stream

This stream uses WASMOL Schedule 3 and is for the subclass 190. Most occupations need a full-time WA employment contract of at least six months. A contract is not required for invited building and construction occupations on that schedule.
Graduate stream

You studied in Western Australia for at least two years and finished a Certificate III or higher at a WA institution. The occupation must be on the Graduate occupation list. You need evidence of two years of full-time study and of living in WA.

blocks.x: Lodge your Expression of Interest, then submit the Registration of Interest in the Migration Tasmania gateway. The gateway tells you if you meet the minimum for a pathway and ranks you against other people.

A Gold result can let you apply for nomination straight away. A Green result is invited later in the program year, if places remain. An Orange result may be invited, and people with an Orange Plus attribute are invited before other Orange results.
For 2026–27 Tasmania has 1,250 places for the 190 and 800 places for the 491. Places can be used up before the program year ends.

blocks.x: Employment used for Gold, Green or Orange Plus must meet the priority income level of AUD 57,000 a year, or a base rate of AUD 28.85 an hour. Do not count overtime, penalty rates or casual loading.
Tasmanian Skilled Employment

You are working in Tasmania. The job, the hours and how long you have worked decide whether you can claim a Gold, Green or Orange attribute. Gold employment includes a job of at least 30 hours a week. Teaching and health roles can reach a strong attribute sooner than other jobs. Read the current attribute table. It is more detailed than a single “six months or nine months” rule.
Tasmanian Skilled Graduate
You finished a qualifying CRICOS course in Tasmania and you meet the study and residence period for that pathway. Work in Tasmania can still decide your rank.
Tasmanian Established Resident
This is for people who have lived in Tasmania for a longer period and can show they have settled there. Check the current residence period on the Migration Tasmania page.

faqs.a: No. Tasmania ranks Registrations of Interest. Gold and Green results are invited ahead of Orange.

faqs.q: What if my points are short for a 190?
faqs.a: The 491 adds 15 points and the 190 adds 5. The 491 can be the visa that gets you to 65 points. Tasmania still has to invite you, and you must meet a 491 pathway.

faqs.q: Can I count overtime toward the income level?
faqs.a: No. The priority income level uses your base pay. Overtime, penalty rates and casual loading are left out.

seo.title: ACT State Nomination and the Canberra Matrix | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: How ACT nomination works through the Canberra Matrix, including 2026–27 fees and how Canberra residents are ranked.
seo.h1: ACT state nomination for the 190 and 491

hero.badge: State nomination, 190 and 491
hero.h1: ACT state nomination for the 190 and 491
intro: The Australian Capital Territory nominates skilled workers who want to live in Canberra. You lodge a SkillSelect Expression of Interest, then a Canberra Matrix.
The Matrix is the ACT’s way of taking expressions of interest. It is not the Home Affairs points test. You must be able to prove every point you claim.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: 600 for 2026–27, as published by the ACT. This can be updated.
200 for 2026–27, as published by the ACT. This can be updated.
AUD 25, or AUD 27.50 including GST. Pay within 7 days or the Matrix lapses.
AUD 325, or AUD 357.50 including GST, for a 190 or a 491.

blocks.x: The Matrix scores things such as skilled work, English, qualifications, time lived or studied in the ACT, investment and close family in Canberra. A high score does not guarantee an invitation. The ACT invites the highest ranked Matrix in each occupation, and it can prefer critical skill occupations.

Canberra residents are invited more often than people overseas, but overseas applicants can still be invited. The ACT does not move you up the list because your visa is about to expire or because you are about to turn 45.

A Matrix is valid for six months. You can update it before it expires and extend it to 12 months. An update is treated as a new submission for ranking. There is no fee to edit it, but each new Matrix submission has its own fee.
Small business owners and people with a doctorate can have their own pathway rules. Read the ACT criteria for the pathway you use.

items.x: Under 45, at least 65 points on the Home Affairs test, and at least competent English.
A valid positive skills assessment.
For the occupation-list pathway, your occupation is on the ACT list.
You meet the pathway you select, such as Canberra resident, overseas applicant, doctorate or small business owner.
You can prove every Matrix claim at the date you submit or last update the Matrix.

blocks.x: The main groups are Canberra residents and overseas applicants. Within those groups, the ACT looks at small business owners, critical skill occupations and other occupations separately.
Do not assume a 491 Matrix is assessed before a 190. Recent rounds have invited 190 applicants while issuing few or no 491 invitations. Check the latest invitation round on the ACT website.
The whole of the ACT is the nominating area. It is not the same test as a regional postcode in New South Wales or Victoria.

items.x: Lodge a SkillSelect EOI and check you meet the ACT pathway rules.
Submit the Canberra Matrix and pay within 7 days.
Wait for an invitation round. Dates are tentative and can move.
If invited, lodge the nomination within the time on the invitation and pay the nomination fee.
After nomination, lodge the visa with Home Affairs.

blocks.x: This page was checked in November 2026. Lists, fees and the number of places change. Read the state website before you apply. A nomination is not a visa. The Department of Home Affairs decides the visa.
Canberra Matrix: AUD 25, or AUD 27.50 including GST. If you do not pay within 7 days, the submission lapses and is not ranked.
Nomination application: AUD 325, or AUD 357.50 including GST, for either a 190 or a 491. Fees are not refunded except in limited cases, such as a payment made in error.
These figures were on the ACT fee table in July 2026. Check [ACT Migration fees](https://www.act.gov.au/migration/resources/act-migration-application-fees) before you pay.
These visas and tools sit next to a state nomination.

items.x: [Skilled Nominated visa (190)](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190). Permanent. Nomination adds 5 points.

[Skilled Work Regional visa (491)](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491). Provisional, up to 5 years. Nomination adds 15 points. You live and work in a regional area.
[Permanent residence after a 491 (191)](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191).

[Postcode Checker](/postcode-checker). See if a suburb counts as regional.
[Book an appointment](/book-an-appointment).

blocks.x: Other states and territories

items.x: [Victoria](/migrate-to-australia/victoria-state-nomination)
[New South Wales](/migrate-to-australia/nsw-state-nomination)
[Queensland](/migrate-to-australia/queensland-state-nomination)
[Western Australia](/migrate-to-australia/western-australia-state-nomination)
[South Australia](/south-australia-state-nomination)
[Tasmania](/migrate-to-australia/tasmania-state-nomination)
[Northern Territory](/migrate-to-australia/northern-territory-state-nomination)

faqs.q: Is the Canberra Matrix the same as a Registration of Interest?
faqs.a: It does the same job. You do not lodge a separate ROI. You lodge the Matrix after your SkillSelect EOI.

faqs.q: Do I have to live in Canberra already?
faqs.a: No. Overseas applicants can be invited. Canberra residents are usually ranked ahead of them.

faqs.q: Will a high Matrix score get me an invitation?
faqs.a: Only if you rank high enough in your occupation and places remain. The ACT will not tell you your chance before a round.
