seo.title: Northern Territory State Nomination (190 and 491) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: NT nomination for 2026–27 is closed for most people. See the limited 491 exceptions and how a direct application works.
seo.h1: Northern Territory state nomination for the 190 and 491

hero.badge: State nomination, 190 and 491
hero.h1: Northern Territory state nomination for the 190 and 491
intro: The Northern Territory nominates for the 190 and 491 visas. Unlike most states, it does not invite you from SkillSelect. If your stream is open, you apply directly to the NT after you lodge an Expression of Interest.
For 2026–27 the NT has enough applications. New 190 applications are closed. Offshore streams are closed. A 491 application is accepted only in limited cases.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Open only by exception, for some onshore NT graduates and NT residents.
If you are nominated for a 491, you are expected to live and work in the NT for at least 3 years.

blocks.x: The NT has said it cannot promise a nomination before your visa expires. If your visa is close to its end date, get advice and stay lawful. A nomination application does not give you a bridging visa.
The NT does not rank people by points score. You still need at least 65 points for the visa, including the points the nomination would add.

When a stream is open, you must show a genuine plan to live and work in the NT. The NT also asks you to show you have enough money to settle. Check the current amounts on the NT site. Do not rely on an old dollar figure.
These are the usual rules when a stream is open. They do not reopen a closed stream.

items.x: Under 45 when the NT nominates you.
A valid positive skills assessment for an occupation on the list for your stream.
At least 65 points and at least competent English, unless your assessing authority asks for a higher score.
Enough settlement funds for your household, at the amounts the NT publishes at the time you apply.

blocks.x: What is still open
A new 491 application is accepted only if you are in Australia, you meet the NT Graduate or NT Resident criteria, and one of these dates falls on or before 30 September 2027:

items.x: Your substantive visa expires on or before that date, and you cannot apply for a subclass 485.
You turn 45 on or before that date.
You have a birthday on or before that date that drops your 491 points below 65.

blocks.x: Meeting one of those dates does not mean you will be nominated. The 190 and every offshore stream stay closed.
Streams, when they are open

items.x: NT Graduate: you finished two academic years of full-time study at an NT institution, and you meet the work or job-search test for that stream.

NT Resident: you have lived in the NT and worked full-time for an NT employer for the period that stream requires. The 190 period is longer than the 491 period. Check the current months before you apply.
Offshore priority occupations: your occupation must be on the Northern Territory Offshore Migration Occupations List. This stream is closed.
Read the NT update and confirm your stream is actually open.
If you are in the 491 exception group, check the graduate or resident test and your points with the [PR Points Calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator).
Lodge a SkillSelect EOI that selects the Northern Territory.
Apply online to the NT with evidence of residence, work and settlement funds.
If the NT nominates you, lodge the visa with Home Affairs within the time on the invitation.

blocks.x: This page was checked in November 2026. Lists, fees and the number of places change. Read the state website before you apply. A nomination is not a visa. The Department of Home Affairs decides the visa.
Check the current NT nomination charge on the Northern Territory migration website. Do not pay an agent or a third party a “holding” fee for a closed stream.
The Home Affairs visa charge is separate and applies only if you are invited to lodge the visa.
These visas and tools sit next to a state nomination.

items.x: [Temporary Graduate visa (485)](/migrate-to-australia/temporary-graduate-visa-subclass-485). Relevant if your student visa is ending and you may not be in the NT exception group.
[Skilled Nominated visa (190)](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-nominated-visa-subclass-190). Permanent. Nomination adds 5 points.

[Skilled Work Regional visa (491)](/migrate-to-australia/skilled-work-regional-provisional-visa-subclass-491). Provisional, up to 5 years. Nomination adds 15 points. You live and work in a regional area.
[Permanent residence after a 491 (191)](/migrate-to-australia/permanent-residence-skilled-regional-visa-subclass-191).
[PR Points Calculator](/migrate-to-australia/pr-point-calculator). Estimate your Home Affairs score.
[Occupation Finder](/occupation-finder). Find your code and assessing authority.
[Skill assessment](/skill-assessment). You need a positive assessment before most states will look at you.
[Postcode Checker](/postcode-checker). See if a suburb counts as regional.
[Book an appointment](/book-an-appointment).

blocks.x: Other states and territories

items.x: [Victoria](/migrate-to-australia/victoria-state-nomination)
[New South Wales](/migrate-to-australia/nsw-state-nomination)
[Queensland](/migrate-to-australia/queensland-state-nomination)
[Western Australia](/migrate-to-australia/western-australia-state-nomination)
[South Australia](/south-australia-state-nomination)
[Tasmania](/migrate-to-australia/tasmania-state-nomination)
[Australian Capital Territory](/migrate-to-australia/act-state-nomination)

faqs.q: Is NT nomination open?
faqs.a: Mostly no. New 190 and offshore applications are closed. Some onshore 491 applicants can still apply if they meet a published exception.

faqs.q: Does the NT pick the highest points?
faqs.a: No. The NT does not rank applicants by points. You still need at least 65 points for the visa.

faqs.q: Will the NT nominate me before my visa expires?
faqs.a: It does not promise that. If your visa is expiring, ask a registered agent about other options and stay lawful.

seo.title: Business Visitor Visa (600) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: The Business Visitor stream of the subclass 600 visa is for short business visits. It does not let you work for an Australian business.
seo.h1: Business Visitor stream of the Visitor visa (600)

hero.badge: Visitor visa, subclass 600
hero.h1: Business Visitor stream of the Visitor visa (600)
intro: This stream is for people outside Australia who need to come for business visitor activities. It is not a work visa.
You can make enquiries, look at or sign a contract, or go to a conference. You cannot work for an Australian business or sell to the public.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: Outside Australia. You must also be outside Australia when the visa is decided.
Usually up to 3 months. A longer stay is uncommon.
AUD 250 for each applicant. Check the current pricing table.
Not allowed, apart from the business visitor activities listed below.

blocks.x: Home Affairs treats these as business visitor activities:

items.x: Make general business or employment enquiries.
Look into, negotiate, sign or review a business contract.
Go to a conference, trade fair or seminar. The organisers must not pay you to take part.
Take part in an official government visit.
Do these things and also visit as a tourist.

blocks.x: You must be a genuine visitor and plan to leave at the end of your stay. You need enough money for the trip and your ticket onward, and you must meet health and character requirements.

items.x: Work for an Australian business, or provide services to one.
Sell goods or services to the public.
Do a normal job in Australia.

blocks.x: Condition 8101, no work, is usually on this visa. The business visitor activities above are the exception.

For applications made on or after 28 November 2026, condition 8503 (no further stay) must be imposed. That stops most new visa applications while you are in Australia. It does not stop you leaving and applying from outside Australia, if you are eligible for that other visa.

items.x: Check that your reason is a business visitor activity, not a job.
Collect evidence of the purpose, your funds, your ties at home, and what you will do in Australia.
Lodge online in ImmiAccount while you are outside Australia. A paper form is only used if the Department tells you to use one.
Give biometrics if you are asked.
Travel after the visa is granted, and leave within the stay period on the grant.

blocks.x: Charges and conditions change. Check the Department of Home Affairs website before you apply. This page is general information.

sections.name: Common refusal reasons
sections.h2: Common reasons these applications are refused

blocks.x: A business visitor visa is refused when the trip looks like work.

items.x: **The activities are productive work,** not meetings, negotiations or a conference.
**You will be paid by an Australian business** for work done here.
**The letter from the business** is vague about dates and who you will meet.
**You do not look like a genuine temporary entrant.**

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record. If you already have a refusal letter, read [visa refusal](/appeals/visa-refusal) and check the deadline before you reapply.
A business visitor stream is still a visitor visa.

items.x: **8101.** You must not work. Business meetings are allowed. Doing the job is not.
**8201** limits study to three months.
**8503** can still be imposed.
**A 482 or 400** is the visa for people who will actually work.

blocks.x: The numbers on your grant letter control what you can do. If a condition is breached, the visa can be cancelled. See [visa cancellation](/appeals/visa-cancellation) and, if you have a notice, [notice of intention to consider cancellation](/appeals/notice-of-intention-to-consider-cancellation).

items.x: [Visitor visa (600) overview](/visitor-visa/visitor-visa-600)
[Frequent Traveller stream](/visitor-visa/visitor-600-frequent-traveller)
[eVisitor (651)](/visitor-visa/evisitor-651)
[Electronic Travel Authority (601)](/visitor-visa/electronic-travel-authority-601)
[Book an appointment](/book-an-appointment)

faqs.q: Can I work on a Business Visitor visa?
faqs.a: No. You can only do the business visitor activities Home Affairs lists, such as meetings, contract talks and conferences. You cannot work for an Australian business.

faqs.q: How long can I stay?
faqs.a: Usually up to 3 months. The grant letter states the period. A longer stay is not the usual grant.

faqs.q: Will condition 8503 be on my visa?
faqs.a: For a Business Visitor application made on or after 28 November 2026, yes. It must be imposed. It limits applications you can make while you are in Australia.

seo.title: Frequent Traveller Visa (600) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: The Frequent Traveller stream is a long visitor visa for citizens of China, Timor-Leste and listed ASEAN countries. Each stay is still short.
seo.h1: Frequent Traveller stream of the Visitor visa (600)

hero.badge: Visitor visa, subclass 600
hero.h1: Frequent Traveller stream of the Visitor visa (600)
intro: This stream is for people who travel to Australia often. The visa can be valid for up to 10 years. Each stay is still short.
It is only for citizens of listed countries. You apply from outside Australia.

head: Fact
Detail
rows: No more than 12 months in any 24-month period.
AUD 1,845 for each applicant. Check the current pricing table.

blocks.x: You must hold a passport from one of these countries, and the passport must show you are a citizen of that country:

items.x: People’s Republic of China
Brunei
Cambodia
Indonesia
Laos
Malaysia
Philippines
Singapore
Thailand
Vietnam
Timor-Leste

blocks.x: You apply from outside Australia, and you must be outside Australia when the visa is decided. You need a genuine reason to visit for tourism, family or business visitor activities, enough money, and ties that show you will leave.

items.x: You cannot stay more than 3 months on one entry.
You cannot be in Australia for more than 12 months in any 24-month period.
Condition 8503 (no further stay) is on this stream. You generally cannot apply for another visa while you are in Australia.
Business activities are limited to the same visitor activities as the [Business Visitor stream](/visitor-visa/visitor-600-business-visitor). You cannot work for an Australian business.

blocks.x: Some citizens of Timor-Leste pay a lower charge. Check the Home Affairs pricing table before you pay.

items.x: Confirm your passport is on the list above.
Prepare evidence of why you travel often, your funds, your job or business at home, and your plans.
Book biometrics if the application asks for them.
Lodge online in ImmiAccount while you are outside Australia.
On each trip, leave within the stay limit and keep track of your total time in Australia.

blocks.x: Charges and conditions change. Check the Department of Home Affairs website before you apply. This page is general information.

sections.name: Common refusal reasons
sections.h2: Common reasons these applications are refused

blocks.x: Frequent traveller grants are refused when the passport, the travel history or the need for repeat visits is not accepted.

items.x: **Your passport is not in a group** the stream is open to.
**Previous travel** does not show you comply with visitor conditions.
**The reason for multiple visits** is not explained.
**The stay pattern** would breach the 12-in-18 limit.

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record. If you already have a refusal letter, read [visa refusal](/appeals/visa-refusal) and check the deadline before you reapply.

items.x: [Visitor visa (600) overview](/visitor-visa/visitor-visa-600)
[Business Visitor stream](/visitor-visa/visitor-600-business-visitor)
[eVisitor (651)](/visitor-visa/evisitor-651)
[Book an appointment](/book-an-appointment)

faqs.q: Can I stay longer than 3 months?
faqs.a: No. Each entry is capped at 3 months, and your total time in Australia cannot be more than 12 months in any 24-month period.

faqs.q: Can any nationality apply?
faqs.a: No. Only citizens of the countries listed on this page, using a passport from that country.

faqs.q: Can I apply in Australia?
faqs.a: No. You must be outside Australia when you apply and when the visa is decided.

/family-visa/partner-visa.name: Partner Visas
/family-visa/partner-visa.pageType: Hub page for partner and prospective marriage visas

seo.title: Partner Visas (820, 801, 309, 100 and 300) | Bansal Immigration
seo.description: Compare onshore and offshore partner visas and the prospective marriage visa. De facto evidence, sponsor limits, condition 8503 and the two-stage process.

hero.badge: Registered migration agents, Melbourne and Adelaide
intro: A partner visa lets the spouse or de facto partner of an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen live in Australia. You apply for the temporary visa and the permanent visa together. Where the applicant is when you lodge decides which subclasses you use.

blocks.x: Most couples do not choose between five visas in the abstract. They choose based on where the applicant is, and whether they are already married, de facto, or engaged and still to marry.

head: Situation
Temporary visa
Permanent visa
Where the applicant must be
rows: Married or de facto, applicant outside Australia
Married or de facto, applicant in Australia
In Australia, on a visa that allows the application
Engaged, and you will marry in Australia

blocks.x: You pay one visa application charge for the temporary and permanent partner stages. It is one of the higher charges. Check the Department of Home Affairs [current visa pricing table](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/fees-and-charges/current-visa-pricing) before you lodge. The prospective marriage visa has its own charge, and the partner visa lodged after the wedding is a new application.

sections.name: Relationship rules
sections.h2: Marriage, de facto and the 12-month rule

blocks.x: A married couple needs a marriage that is valid under Australian law. A de facto couple needs to have been in the relationship for at least 12 months before lodgement, unless an exception applies. The usual exceptions are a child of the relationship, or a relationship registered with an Australian state or territory that registers relationships.

You must have met in person as adults. Online contact alone is not enough. For a prospective marriage visa you must also intend to marry, and the wedding has to be able to take place within the visa period.
Case officers look at four kinds of evidence, taken together:

items.x: **Financial.** Joint accounts, transfers, shared rent, who pays which bills, and how you support each other if you live apart.
**Household.** Where you live, or how you run a household across two countries. Separate addresses need an explanation, not a gap.
**Social.** Photos, travel, messages, and statements from people who know you as a couple. A pile of wedding photos without anything else is weak.
**Commitment.** How long you have been together, your plans, wills, and what you do when you are apart.

blocks.x: A long-distance couple can succeed. The file has to show the relationship is genuine and continuing, not only that you intend it to become one later.

The sponsor is the Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen. Home Affairs assesses the sponsor, including police checks. Some offences, including family violence offences, can stop a sponsorship.

items.x: A person can usually sponsor only a limited number of partners in their lifetime, and there is normally a five-year gap between sponsorships.
The sponsor gives a financial undertaking to support the applicant.

If the relationship ends, the application does not always end with it. There are specific rules where the sponsor has died, where there is a child of the relationship, and where the applicant or a family member has suffered family violence.

Children of the applicant are not automatic. A child of a temporary partner visa holder may need a [dependent child visa (445)](/family-visa/dependent-child-visa). A child of a citizen or resident uses a [child visa](/family-visa/child-visa-subclass-101).

sections.name: Two stages
sections.h2: The two stages, and waiting in Australia

blocks.x: For 309/100 and 820/801 you lodge both stages at the start. The Department usually looks at the permanent stage about two years after lodgement, to see that the relationship is still genuine. You do not pay the visa application charge again for that second look.

If you apply in Australia on a substantive visa, you usually receive a bridging visa. Work rights on that bridging visa depend on the visa you held. A visitor visa often leads to a bridging visa with condition 8101 (no work) until it is changed. Read [Bridging Visa A](/bridging-return-visas/bridging-visa-a-010). Leaving Australia on a Bridging Visa A usually ends it. A [Bridging Visa B](/bridging-return-visas/bridging-visa-b-020) is the travel visa, and you must get it before you leave.
If you apply outside Australia, you usually wait outside. A visit while the 309 is processing does not move the file onshore.

sections.name: Common refusal reasons
sections.h2: Common reasons these applications are refused

blocks.x: Partner visas are refused on evidence and on visa status. The size of the charge is a reason to check both before you lodge.

items.x: **The relationship evidence does not cover the four areas,** or it conflicts with travel records and earlier visa applications.
**De facto time is under 12 months** and there is no registered relationship and no child of the relationship.
**You have not met in person** as adults.
**The sponsor is not eligible,** because of a previous sponsorship, character, or because they are not usually resident in Australia.

**Condition 8503 (no further stay)** or a similar condition makes an onshore 820 application invalid. A [waiver](/appeals/waiver-request) has to be approved first. Marriage or the relationship itself is often not accepted as the reason for a waiver.
**The applicant is unlawful** and Schedule 3 is not met. There is a limited discretion. Do not assume it will be exercised.
**The prospective marriage visa** is refused because the wedding is not planned in a real way, or the couple do not marry within condition 8519 and do not lodge the partner visa in time.

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record. If you already have a refusal letter, read [visa refusal](/appeals/visa-refusal) and check the deadline before you reapply.
Partner visas are not employer visas. Condition 8607 does not apply. The conditions that matter are the ones on the visa you hold now, and a small set on the prospective marriage visa.

items.x: **8503 No further stay.** Common on visitor visas. It stops an onshore partner application unless it is waived. Check VEVO before you book a flight to apply in Australia.
**820 then 801, and 309 then 100.** After the temporary visa is granted you can usually work and study. Medicare enrolment follows the grant, not the lodgement.
**8519 on a subclass 300.** You must marry the sponsoring partner within the visa period. If you do not, the visa can end and the partner pathway stops.
**Bridging visa conditions.** Until the temporary partner visa is granted, condition 8101 (no work) may apply. Do not work in breach of it.

**Second stage.** If the relationship has ended, get advice before you ignore a Department letter. Family violence, a child, or the death of the sponsor are specific claims with their own evidence rules.

blocks.x: The numbers on your grant letter control what you can do. If a condition is breached, the visa can be cancelled. See [visa cancellation](/appeals/visa-cancellation) and, if you have a notice, [notice of intention to consider cancellation](/appeals/notice-of-intention-to-consider-cancellation).

items.x: [Partner visa onshore, temporary (820)](/family-visa/partner-provisional-visa-subclass-820)
[Partner visa onshore, permanent (801)](/family-visa/partner-permanent-visa-subclass-801)
[Partner visa offshore, temporary (309)](/family-visa/partner-provisional-visa-subclass-309)
[Partner visa offshore, permanent (100)](/family-visa/partner-permanent-visa-subclass-100)
[Prospective marriage visa (300)](/family-visa/prospective-marriage-visa-subclass-300)
[No further stay waiver](/appeals/waiver-request)
[Family visas](/family-visa)

faqs.q: Do we apply for the permanent visa later?
faqs.a: For 820/801 and 309/100 you lodge both stages together and pay once. The permanent stage is assessed about two years after lodgement. The prospective marriage visa is different: you marry first, then lodge a partner visa.

faqs.q: We have lived together for eight months. Can we apply?
faqs.a: A de facto relationship usually needs 12 months, unless you register the relationship in an Australian state or territory that allows it, or you have a child together. Marriage does not need the 12 months.

faqs.q: Can I apply for an 820 on a tourist visa?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the tourist visa does not have condition 8503 or another condition that blocks further applications. If it does, you need a waiver first, and a waiver is often refused when the reason is the relationship.

faqs.q: Can I work while the application is processed?
faqs.a: Only if your bridging visa or current visa allows it. A bridging visa that follows a visitor visa often has condition 8101, which means no work.

faqs.q: What if we break up?
faqs.a: It depends on the stage and the reason. There are specific provisions for family violence, a child of the relationship, and the death of the sponsor. Contact us before you withdraw anything.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee the visa?
faqs.a: No. Only the Department of Home Affairs decides.

cta.title: Not sure whether to apply onshore or offshore?
cta.text: Bring the applicant's visa grant letter. Condition 8503 changes the answer.
